# Making and reviewing lessons

233 learnings. Each says where it came from and what argues against it. [What a perfect question is](../PERFECT-QUESTION.md) collects the criteria by facet, and [How to generate perfect questions](../GENERATING.md) collects the methods by stage.

### Fit the most constrained real screen

Fit the text, the task and the controls on one screen without page scroll at the most constrained size learners really use, measured on a real device. A device survey made 1366×640, the usable page on an HD school laptop, the primary layout, with 1180×760 for a landscape tablet.

A device survey for a desktop-first Grade 9 design took 1366×640, the usable page on an HD school laptop, as the primary layout because it is the most common and most constrained real school screen, with 1180×760 for a landscape tablet second. Its test is that if the text pane, the question pane and the footer fit there with no page scroll, the design works anywhere larger, and it asks for the usable height to be checked with window.innerHeight on a real school laptop before the grid is locked. The prototype's screens are built at both sizes.

Quoted:

- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md` (39): “This is the most common and most constrained real school screen.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md` (39): “If text pane, question pane and footer fit here with no page scroll, the design works anywhere larger.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md` (25): “Check this with `window.innerHeight` on a real school Chromebook before locking the grid.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md` (24): “On a 1366×768 Chromebook that leaves roughly 1366×630–660 of usable page.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/prototype/README.md` (33): “Screens are built for 1366×640 (the usable page on an HD Chromebook) and 1180×760 (a landscape iPad).”

Against: The survey says "I found no authoritative figure for the height lost to Chrome's tab strip, the toolbar and the ChromeOS shelf." (othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/design/grade-9/research/edtech-desktop-design.md, line 23), so the usable height rests on a working assumption of roughly 1366×630–660 (line 24).

### Fixed lesson parts, flexible time

Give every lesson the same parts in the same order, and change how much time each part gets rather than whether it appears. In one Grade 9 design, independent practice takes 20% of a first-encounter lesson and 65% of an expert one, while every part still appears.

A Grade 9 lesson design specification says every lesson contains every component, in a fixed order, and that the time each gets changes with the lesson: components are modules of variable length, not fixed slides, and its profiles move independent practice from 20% of a first-encounter lesson to 65% of an expert one (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, lines 29, 196, 218, 222 and 293). A Grade 3 reading course's lesson design likewise fixes the lesson's shape and lets only its block of tasks flex (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, line 115). Neither design reports an outcome.

Quoted:

- `g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md` (29): “Every lesson contains every component, in this order. The time each component gets changes with the lesson (see Section 10).”
- `g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md` (196): “Every lesson contains every component, but the time each one gets changes with the lesson.”
- `g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md` (293): “Components are modules of variable length, not fixed slides.”
- `g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md` (218): “| **A. First encounter** | 1.1 | 10 | 30 | 30 | 20 | 10 |”
- `g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md` (222): “| **E. Expert** | Whole-text argument | 10 | 5 | 5 | 65 | 15 |”
- `g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx` (115): “The lesson shape is fixed: video, read with purpose, a block of tasks, the Modelling Moment, Part 3, closing, doors. Only the task block flexes.”

Against: Neither shape is rigid: the Grade 3 design lets whole parts give way when a child is slow, its Magic Doors first (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 352 and 358), and in the Grade 9 specification only unit-opening lessons begin with the unit video and review lessons change the form of guided practice (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, lines 29 and 224).

### Hold a taught word in place

Keep a word being taught in the same place through every stage of its routine, reserving room from the start for any control that appears later. A taught word shifted about 70px sideways when its speaker icon appeared.

A supplied UI review saw a taught word shift about 70px sideways when its speaker icon appeared (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md`, line 30). The project found that the 48px speaker was inserted only at the routine's second stage, and reserved its footprint from arrival so the word keeps its position (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md`, line 15). A rendered fixture verified identical word position and size for all five scoped words at the arrival, sound-out and completed stages (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 28).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/aladdin-p1-ui-review.reference.md` (30): “Content also moves *within* a screen: on `/p2` the word "betrayal" shifts about 70px sideways when the speaker icon appears, and the forward pill moves down roughly 55px across three steps.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/REVIEW-MAPPING.md` (15): “Vocab inserts a48px speaker only atstage2. Reserve its footprint from arrival; retain same word position.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md` (28): “It verifies all five scoped vocabulary words at arrival, sound-out and completed stages: identical word x/y/width/height;48×72 reserve; hidden control before its authored stage;48px target; non-overlapping visible label; visible text contained in its accessible name.”

Against: The proof is a component fixture, not the live lesson: "Its screenshot is illustrative component evidence, not an acceptance screenshot of a runtime lesson." (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/gold-standard/STYLE-IMPLEMENTATION-by-residual.md`, line 30).

### Neighbouring courses must really differ

A course for one level must differ from the course for the level beside it in more than its lesson list, difficulty and units, because near-copies share their weaknesses.

The course-plan agents made a sibling clone a blocking finding: a design whose only differences from the nearest sibling are lesson spines, difficulty and units fails review (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md`, lines 99-101). Every design first loads a grade-band profile of the dimensions that must differ by grade, among them text band, stamina, genre split, item formats, depth-of-knowledge mix and gate design (the same file, lines 89-91). The rule answered a standing concern that courses for neighbouring grades built under the same guidance were so alike that one rejection would bring the rest for the same underlying reasons (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`).

Quoted:

- `ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md` (99-101): “**"Sibling clone" is a blocking red-team finding class**: a design whose only deltas from the nearest sibling are lesson spines/difficulty/units fails review”
- `ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md` (89-91): “dimensions that MUST differ by grade (axis, decoding share, text band, stamina, schema progression, genre split, item formats, DOK mix, gate design, anchor)”
- `ti-courseplans-audit/docs/grade-band-profiles.md` (7): “rejected for the same underlying reasons. We're just failing in parallel.”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/sources/STAAR-RLA-BLUEPRINT.md` (71): “the current live AlphaWrite Paragraphs G4/G5 are byte-identical — the failure mode to avoid”
- `incept-package-hub/course-packages/courses/g7-reading/releases/2026-07-26/artifacts/Grade 7 Reading - BrainLift.md` (469): “G7 is **not** "G6 with harder text," and it is **not** "a lighter G8."”

Against: The joint rejection is a stated concern, not an observed outcome.

### No dead ends for the learner

No state, such as a reload mid-step, a failed 3D or media part, or help that has run out, may leave a learner without a way on. A word-web row whose give-after-two-misses had run out of words is released rather than left with nothing to add.

In a 3D version of the Grade 9 lessons, a reload between a lesson's last task and its return to the learning question once left a dead screen; the closing step now counts the task done once its final answer is saved, and finishes a step a reload left between the last reply and the save (`othello-archive/src/steps/Close.tsx`, lines 74-75 and 198). Its reading page sends the learner on when a stage fails, its unit film falls back to a still picture when the 3D fails, and a word-web row that has run out of words to give is released instead of stalling (`othello-archive/src/steps/Reading.tsx`, line 19; `othello-archive/src/film/Film.tsx`, line 135; `othello-archive/src/retrieval/Recall.tsx`, line 173).

Quoted:

- `othello-archive/src/steps/Close.tsx` (75): “which the last task only sets after the learning-question return, so a reload in between left a dead screen)”
- `othello-archive/src/steps/Close.tsx` (198): “a reload between the last reply and the save: finish it now (never a dead end)”
- `othello-archive/src/steps/Reading.tsx` (19): “never strand the student behind a stage that failed”
- `othello-archive/src/film/Film.tsx` (135): “3D failed, showing the still”
- `othello-archive/src/retrieval/Recall.tsx` (173): “row is released instead of leaving the student with nothing to add (A-329: never loop, never dead-end)”

Against: none found

### One interface across lessons

Give every lesson in a course the same controls and components, so lessons differ in content and structure, not in how they work.

Feedback on the reading course asked for interface standardization among other changes (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`). A later ruling required every other lesson to follow the reference lesson's interface to the tee, with no variations. A census of the page's interface classes confirmed that a rebuilt lesson differed, and the following lessons were rebuilt keeping their own structure while their components were made to look exactly like the reference's (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0222-g3-l4-l1-parity-rebuild-2026-09-17-to-21.qmd`).

### Reviewer controls leave no evidence

Controls for previewing or reviewing a lesson, such as free navigation, answer reveal and reset, leave mastery, rewards, completion and unlocks exactly as they were.

The reading course plans' quality checklist marks reviewer isolation as universal: free navigation, answer reveal, reset and reviewer-only controls leave mastery, reward, completion and unlock records unchanged, so exploring a course can't mint a learner's achievements or alter progression (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q011). The practice layer's app requirements include a reviewer mode that unlocks lessons without minting mastery evidence, and stamps earned under compressed calendars are marked non-evidence (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd` (34): “Free navigation, answer reveal, reset, and reviewer-only controls leave mastery, reward, completion, and unlock records unchanged.”

### Unreached steps take no input

Make every step the learner hasn't reached unreachable by any input, keyboard included, not just faded from view. After the fix, ten test groups checked that a later task stays inert until the current quote is judged.

On a staged page, tabbing on from the current quote field moved focus into a later task's text box that the learner had not reached (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json`, line 2500). Future steps were hidden with opacity and pointer settings only, and the fields inside them were not disabled. The repair made the later task inert until the current quote is judged, checked in ten test groups and a corrected keyboard sequence (line 2510).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (2500): “Focus enters the unreached extra-thinking textarea.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (2500): “Default staged branch prints future bk-stepblock waiting children using opacity and pointer-events only.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (2500): “Native focus JSON confirms disabled:false inside waiting parent.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (2510): “future inference inert until actual current quote judged.”

Against: none found

### Vary the learner's moves

Give each interactive move in a course its own action, and never run three moves of one kind in a row, so the moves don't feel repetitive. A static gate fails a course in which one verb is used twice or three moves of one kind come in a row.

Review feedback on a 3D version of the Grade 9 lessons noted stage moves repeating across lessons, such as taking a mask off and putting it back (`othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, lines 8-9). Every move now needs a verb unique in the course, and a static gate fails the course when a verb is used twice or when three moves in a row in one lesson are of one kind, click, drag or choose (`othello-archive/src/scene/moments/kit.ts`, line 35; `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, lines 8 and 13).

Quoted:

- `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs` (8): “the same verb is used twice in the course”
- `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs` (9): “take mask, put mask across lessons”
- `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs` (13): “three moves in a row in one lesson of the same kind (click/drag/choose)”
- `othello-archive/src/scene/moments/kit.ts` (35): “Make a move. Every move needs a course-unique `verb` (the variety gate checks it) and an `expect` (the vision gate).”
- `othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs` (10): “more than 2 mask moves in the course (L1's take-off / put-back pair is the only one)”

Against: The gate allows one deliberate pair, a mask taken off and put back, under a course budget of two mask moves (`othello-archive/scripts/check-moments.mjs`, line 10).

### A check counts what should be there

Give a check an expected count from the content, code or a fixed list, never from what it finds, and fail by name on anything missing or unknown. A test script driving a lesson reported 0 problems while leaving one item unanswered; only an unrelated count, reading 6 of 7, showed it.

A Grade 3 reading build's rulebook found that an assertion over everything a walker found is true whenever it finds nothing: after an interaction changed shape, a walker reported every gate answered with 0 problems while leaving an item unanswered, and only an unrelated count of answered items, reading 6 of 7, showed it. The fix has the walk say how many items it reached and compares that with a number taken from the content, never from the walk's own tally, and ends the type dispatch with a branch that names any new item type instead of skipping it. The rulebook generalises that a check walking what it found notices things appearing but never disappearing, so a table of expected things needs assertions in both directions; a Grade 5 course's science gate likewise holds its fixed list of 27 passage IDs apart from the scope ledger, so deleting a row cannot hide a lesson. The Grade 3 package derives its response floors from the player's own call sites and the authored content rather than pinning them, so a response kind the table doesn't know fails by name instead of being under-counted.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (518): “An assertion over "everything the walker found" needs a companion assertion over how many things it”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (765): “anyone noticed was an unrelated downstream assertion counting answered items, which read 6 of 7.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (526): “Take the denominator from the CONTENT, never from the walk's own”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (527-528): “so a newly authored item type is a named problem instead of a silent no-op”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/evidence/science-process.md` (50): “27-ID expectation independently, so deleting a row cannot make a lesson disappear from the check.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (594): “only notice things APPEARING, never things DISAPPEARING.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (601): “both directions; one of them is usually missing.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/CASE-FOR-APPROVAL.md` (186): “The floors are derived, not pinned.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/CASE-FOR-APPROVAL.md` (188): “rather than under-counting silently.”

Against: A count taken from content the delivery code never consults can agree with the bug: "Deriving a count from content the player does not consult is not the conservative choice; it makes the gate agree with the bug." (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md`, lines 622-623).

### A check not run has not passed

A check that never ran, ran on nothing or was out of service has not passed: count it, and anything made while it was down, as failed or unverified. A per-file test gate reported 0 pass and 0 fail because every file lookup missed.

The reading project's staged item standard counts a blind solve that was not run as a fail, not a pass (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/item-quality.md`), and its non-negotiables leave no line blank: absence of evidence is marked unverified, not silence (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/non-negotiables.md`). The course-plan standard the project pinned keeps a contribution with no suitable check pending, states the missing check, and forbids agents to invent a passing verdict (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/docs/standards/course-json/README.md`). A per-file test gate once reported 0 pass and 0 fail because every file lookup missed, and the rule since is to treat a 0/0 verdict as a harness bug until proven otherwise (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd`). Count every empty, invalid, timed-out or unscorable output as failed or unverified too, and make a run over zero items stop with an error.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/item-quality.md` (63-64): “**`NEEDS_LLM_GRADE` (the blind solve not run) is a FAIL, not a pass.**”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/non-negotiables.md` (61): “No line may be left blank; absence of evidence is `UNVERIFIED`, not silence.”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/docs/standards/course-json/README.md` (283-284): “If no suitable check exists, the contribution stays pending and the missing check is stated in the PR. Agents must not invent a passing verdict.”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd` (182): “**Symptom (2026-10-01):** a per-file test gate reported 0 pass / 0 fail.”

### A check's signal must match its finding

Count a fault as caught only when its own check flags the right place, never on a crash or failing run, and fail runs printing failures, whatever their exit code. A validator for a generated question pool printed hard failures while exiting zero, so neither its '71/71 complete' nor exit code zero could admit the pool.

A lesson project's test harness for its content checkers counts a planted fault as caught only when the checker flags the node the test case names; a flag anywhere else is a guess. A dry run of the harness showed that an uncaught exception exits the same way as a finding, so a checker that threw on every input would pass every fault case, and the harness now treats a printed stack trace as a crash whatever the exit code. Separately, a validator for a generated question pool printed hard failures while exiting zero, so its completion count and its exit code were ruled out as an admission test.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/test/run.mjs` (8-9): “A checker that exits 1 but points at the wrong node has not found the defect, it has guessed.”
- `grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/test/run.mjs` (199-201): “An UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION also exits 1 — indistinguishable from "found a defect" by exit code alone, so a checker that throws on every input would pass every positive case.”
- `grade3-reading/curriculum-gen/test/run.mjs` (201-203): “Node prints a stack trace to stderr, which no finding ever does; treat that as a crash regardless of exit code. Found by dry-running this template, not by reasoning about it.”
- `grade3-reading/bias_experiment/experiment-record/evidence/knowledgebot/kb-0132-eppc-bias-experiment-execution-handover.qmd` (122-123): “The validator also prints hard tell failures while exiting zero. Therefore neither “71/71 complete” nor exit code zero is an admission test.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (490): “A negative control must check that the mutation was caught BY THE NAMED ASSERTION, not merely that”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (510-511): “A mutation caught by two assertions establishes that neither is load-bearing”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (499): “WHERE you sample a state is part of the assertion”

Against: Exclusivity is the wrong bar for wide changes: "Wide-reaching mutations (removing an idempotency guard, reverting to the unpatched player) legitimately trip many assertions and exclusivity is the wrong bar for them" (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md`, lines 513-515).

### A closed list of thinking operations

Tag items against a closed, versioned list of thinking operations kept apart from format and knowledge labels, so each item is labelled by the work it demands.

A Grade 5 reading project's taxonomy calibration found that, with knowledge labels admissible as operation tags, verdicts on whether an item's tag matched its work were ill-posed: an evidence item could classify to a format label for selecting evidence instead of the operation of telling supported from unsupported claims. An open vocabulary was rejected on that measurement, and a proposal declares a closed list of operations, versioned with the graph and open to challenge at review, with facts, schemas and format knowledge kept as knowledge rather than operations. It calls the list a design commitment, not a discovery, since reading comprehension has no natural set of operations.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/kc-graph-change-proposal.md` (90-93): “Without a declared closed label set, tag-vs-work verdicts are ill-posed: with knowledge KCs admissible as labels, an evidence item can classify to the format KC `exam_hottext_select_evidence` instead of the cognitive op `disc_supported_vs_unsupported`.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/kc-graph-change-proposal.md` (35-37): “rejected on measurement - ground 2 of the op-taxonomy NO-GO; tag-vs-work verdicts become ill-posed and evidence items classify to format KCs (exam_hottext_select_evidence) instead of cognitive work.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/kc-graph-change-proposal.md` (30-33): “The closed operation vocabulary is a curriculum design commitment, not a discovery: ELA comprehension has no domain-intrinsic operation set, so this list is a choice this build makes, versioned with the graph (graph_version bump + rationale to change it) and challengeable at review.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/JUDGE-CALIBRATION-REPORT.md` (83-84): “As a blocking gate this behavior would false-flag honestly tagged evidence items.”

Against: The closed list is still a proposal (`grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/kc-graph-change-proposal.md`, line 9), and in the same calibration a judge relabelled one honestly tagged evidence item to a neighbouring operation, which as a blocking gate would false-flag such items (`grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/JUDGE-CALIBRATION-REPORT.md`, lines 81-84).

### A debt list that can only shrink

When a new rule meets older content, list each existing breach as debt that warns every run, and fail anything unlisted and any stale entry, so the list only shrinks. One unit never held to the rules written the week it merged entered the list with nineteen sentences over the word ceiling.

A reading engine lists content that predates a rule item by item in one file shared by the validators of those rules. A listed item warns on every run instead of failing, an unlisted breach fails, and an entry that matches nothing fails too, so fixing an item forces its entry out, and a rule with entries is still enforced. It was built when a unit merged from another branch had never been held to rules written that week, with nineteen sentences over the word ceiling, seventeen missing hint-ladder rungs and one taught word owing its reason, and nothing may be added to it just to make a build pass. A draft certification standard in the same project keeps the same kind of list (no-exemption-without-a-cost).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/course-renderer/AGENTS.md` (126-128): “A listed item warns instead of failing, an unlisted one fails, and an entry nothing matches fails too, so fixing something forces its entry to be deleted and the list can only shrink.”
- `grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/README.md` (67-71): “Content that predates a rule is not an exception to it. It goes in [`../../scripts/known-debt.mjs`](../../scripts/known-debt.mjs), listed item by item, where it warns on every run rather than failing the build, and where fixing one forces its entry to be deleted. A rule with entries there is still enforced.”
- `grade3-reading/course-renderer/AGENTS.md` (128-131): “Do not add to it to make a build pass: it exists so a rule can apply to content its author never saw without either rewriting someone else's lesson or scoping the rule down to the grade that happened to be in front of you.”
- `grade3-reading/course-renderer/AGENTS.md` (124-126): “nineteen sentences over the word ceiling, seventeen missing hint-ladder rungs, one taught word owing its off-list reason.”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0217-team-direction-2026-09-09.qmd` (67-68): “known-debt list (can only shrink, never padded to pass a build).”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/judgment-corpus/distilled-src/08-VERIFICATION-DISCIPLINE.md` (44-47): “Content that predates a rule is not an exception — it is listed item by item; the list WARNS on every run instead of failing (so debt stays visible); an unlisted violation still FAILS; an entry nothing currently matches FAILS (an exemption that outlived its cause is a silencer); and the list may only shrink.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/PP-DEFENSE-2026-09-22.md` (68-69): “Pre-existing findings ride `voice-laws-debt.json` with shrink-only semantics: listed warns, unlisted fails, a stale entry fails.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/AGENTS.md` (126-128): “A listed item warns instead of failing, an unlisted one fails, and an entry nothing matches fails too, so fixing something forces its entry to be deleted and the list can only shrink.”

Against: Where content can be regenerated, the opposite rule applies: remake what was made under an old rule instead of serving it. A listed breach still reaches learners, with only a warning, until someone fixes it.

### A difficulty set before use is a prior

Treat any difficulty, threshold or cut score set before learners have answered as a labelled prior, and replace it with live response data. Estimating one item's difficulty with reasonable precision needs at least 100 to 200 responses, and at about 10 students per course even 100 takes 10 to 20 cohorts.

A diagnostic BrainLift worked through on AP courses notes that estimating one item's difficulty with reasonable precision needs at minimum 100-200 responses, that at about 10 students per course it takes 10-20 cohorts to reach 100, and so parameters must come from judgment and structural defaults (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`, lines 382-384). Its cold-start section, drawing on published studies, ranks a model's direct rating as the weakest approach (often r ≈ 0.4–0.6), behind feature-based models (r ≈ 0.7–0.87 with ≥100 calibrated items) and placement against 3–5 calibrated anchors, distrusts predictions that swing under small wording changes, and requires every pre-use value to carry a provenance label such as 'pre-use predicted, N=0' (lines 3172-3196). The reading courses' standard says the same: predicted difficulty is a prior with method, population, provenance and uncertainty, which live data must eventually replace (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/sources/knowledge-bot/kb-0164-g3-v2-feedback-agent-routing.qmd`, lines 97-98). Estimate a pre-use difficulty from item features or calibrated anchors rather than a model's own rating, record its method, sample size and uncertainty, and set no cut score on it.

Against: Both stronger methods need calibrated items that a new course doesn't have, which leaves rubric scoring of difficulty drivers for the cold start (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`, line 3186); and in one assessment bank all 650 items carry assigned, uncalibrated difficulties, so nobody knows how hard any single item actually is for students (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/05_LIMITATIONS.md`, line 11). Simulation suggests a well-built adaptive engine tolerates the guess, keeping reliability at or above 0.85, though with less precision than after calibration. The one internal case offered for it is unsettled: two simulation misses were traced to difficulties assigned by hand rather than estimated from responses (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0080-map-proxy-case-for-approval-2026-07-02-incept-map-proxy-approval-package.qmd`), but a later self-reported run on a bigger bank (786 items vs 650) reported RMSE 3.20 against the earlier 4.12 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0086-round2-feedback-brainlifts-2026-07-09.qmd`). The 200-response line is the doctrine's example, not a calibrated threshold. Simulated students are best used only as a supplementary signal, and the advice to place a new item against calibrated anchors is the BrainLift's own view, with no study cited for it (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0163-cold-start-item-difficulty-estimation.qmd`).

### A new procedure needs its own pages

Rebuild pages copied from a lesson on another procedure around the new procedure's steps, since new wording in old page shapes hides the change of task from learners. After the point where a new skill began, exactly one new presentation type appeared, and every other page reused an earlier shape.

A review of a reading lesson said that everything should change once skill instruction starts, and the response measured it: comparing node types on either side of that point found exactly one new presentation type, and the two pages where the child performs the new skill had the shape of an earlier comprehension check (`grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf`, p.2). The lesson shared node ids with a lesson teaching a different procedure, because the page template had been copied and only its strings changed. It also put five procedure screens on one scrolling page, where the procedure gives each step its own screen and advance button, and its step table fell through to the component that had drawn an earlier story table (the same file, pp.2 and 4). The response found the content faithful to the design but invisible to the child, and planned to give each step its own screen and add the procedure's step rail.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf` (p.2 (pdftotext lines 52-53)): “So exactly one new presentation type appears after the skill starts. Everything else after the boundary reuses the shape the child has already been reading with.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf` (p.2 (pdftotext lines 57-58)): “The page template was copied and the strings were changed.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf` (p.2 (pdftotext lines 81-83)): “It currently compresses five procedure screens into one scrolling page (six stacked question nodes). The procedure gives each step its own screen and its own advance button. This is the biggest single cause of 'feels like a FIND lesson'.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf` (p.1 (pdftotext lines 33-35)): “But the lesson delivers that content through the page shape of a FIND lesson, so a child never experiences the mode change you describe. The pedagogy is present and invisible.”

Against: Lessons must still read as one app: "Procedure differences don't excuse voice differences." (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/arc-audit/SKILL.md`, line 18), and the request itself asked for the change "while reusing UI components where possible." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/Peter-Pan-L4-review-response-2026-08-25.pdf`, p.1). The comparison covers one lesson, and nothing measured whether learners noticed the change of task.

### A quiet failure needs its own detector

Every rule that fails safe by going quiet, such as missing audio playing as silence, needs its own detector, or its failures stay invisible to other checks.

The reading project's rule that a missing clip plays as silence, never as wrong words, made missing audio invisible to every check built around whether the words match, because the rule's failure mode was never instrumented. Its QA notes conclude that a safety rule without a matching detector is a permanent blind spot, and its handover notes say every rule that degrades to quiet needs a detector.

### A quota balances only what it counts

A quota balances only the level it counts, so set and check targets for the standards and formats inside each domain, not only for the domains. One adaptive test came within one item of its domain quotas in every simulated session while its bank held 28 items on one standard against a target of 8.

A reading assessment's simulation held its domain quotas to within one item in 100% of sessions, and its write-up says this does not guarantee balance across the standards inside a domain, which bank composition and the item-selection rule decide (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md`). Its bank held 28 items on one third-grade standard and 19 on another, each against a target of 8, and 31 on a third, 26 of them on prefix meaning (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/reference/CAT_MAP_EXAM_SPEC.md`). Two formats were stocked above their per-form targets as well, so they will be seen more often than intended even though the engine enforces per-session quotas. A cap of two items per standard per session was proposed, not shipped.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md` (284): “Blueprint adherence at the domain level does not guarantee standard-level balance.”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/03_SIMULATION_EVIDENCE.md` (284): “the distribution across RL standards is determined by bank composition and Fisher-information selection”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md` (233): “Domain quota enforcement verified across 1,000 simulated sessions.”

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md` (268): “Three G3 standards are over-represented: RL.3.3 (28 items vs. target 8), RI.3.3 (19 items vs. target 8), and L.3.4 (31 items with 26 marked deprioritized).”

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md` (85): “The bank's MSQ and hot-text counts are above the per-form targets. This does not block delivery — the CAT enforces per-session quotas — but means these formats will be seen more frequently than intended before additional MCQ/EBSR items are added.”

Against: A topic cap limits how often any one topic appears in a session, which the package counts as some mitigation (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/02_ITEM_BANK.md`, line 268), and the over-testing is its expectation, not a measured serving rate. The per-standard counts come from a matrix the same file marks as stale, though it undercounted rather than overcounted (lines 121–132).

### A reference course shows presentation only

Let a reference course inform only interaction and presentation: it never proves a verdict, content correctness or grade fit, and none of its content, numbers or policies carry across.

The Grade 5 reading release uses the Grade 3 player as a presentation reference, not as course authority, and copies none of Grade 3's story content, mascot language, passage chunking, vocabulary count or item policy (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/GRADE_5_REVIEW_NOTES.qmd`, lines 9 and 28-31). Its instruction-review profile gives the reference the role of interaction and presentation reference only, lists criterion verdict, content correctness and grade appropriateness as what it may not prove, and admits a reference-course artifact only in a comparison note, never as verdict evidence (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/generated/instruction-review-profile.json`, lines 116-127 and 156). A Grade 7 BrainLift treats its neighbouring grades the same way: they are method templates, and their numbers are theirs (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g7-reading/releases/2026-07-26/artifacts/Grade 7 Reading - BrainLift.md`, lines 451-453).

### A repeating failure is a fault to find

A failure that repeats across items or retries is a fault, not noise: redrafting or rescoring won't fix it, so rule out broken measurement, find its cause and test it. Nine targeted fixes, each for one specific fault, added 15.1 points to the pass rate.

At 81.9% the AP question work's remaining failures were systematic, not random (`icloud-work/ML learnings/gemini_benchmark_relentless.md`). Of about 40-50 automated iterations most changed nothing, and the nine that worked each removed a specific code or prompt bug behind a specific failing dimension, adding 15.1 points in about 48 hours. The project's diagnostic method goes from the aggregate to the failing dimension and items, then two or three hypotheses and a test that tells them apart, with a catalogue of signatures: a whole unit failing points to wrong scope labels, a whole item type to missing examples, right content on the wrong topic to an ignored constraint, and wrong specifics to invented details (`icloud-work/ML learnings/debugging_methodology.md`). Each time a step was skipped, going from an aggregate straight to a fix, a training run was wasted. Signs of such a failure include a whole item type at zero or all passing, and scores bunched under the pass line. Rule out a broken measurement as well as a broken pipeline.

Quoted:

- `icloud-work/ML learnings/gemini_benchmark_relentless.md` (13): “At 81.9%, the system was generating correct AP questions most of the time. The remaining ~18% failures were not random — they were systematic, patterned failures. The key insight that drove the relentless push: every failure is evidence of a specific, fixable bug.”

Among items that failed every scoring, the evidence does not single out near misses: three of the six that scored 0.7-0.8 every time became triple passes once the writer was given each objective's scope limits and sub-objectives, as did both items with zero scores, while two near misses did not move (`project_richer_rag_resolves_stable_fails.md`, lines 27-35). A failure that repeats can be the judge's own: a '0%' on one item type was 9 real verdicts and 91 timeouts (`feedback_ib_grader_v266_dbq_mcqset_timeout_99pct_at_concurrency_default_2026_06_02.md`, line 11). And a structural failure holds for one judge version and one generator: a grounded generator's document sets passed a later judge 139 of 154 times (`recipe_track_b_openstax_pair_generation.md`, line 67). The lifts were scored by the same grader that picked the best version; a held-out judge agreed on 21 of 24 rescued items, so part of the measured lift may be the picking fitting the grader. A flip is not always a slip: a later change to the same evaluator found that the flips it studied were not noise on clean items but genuine defects in the scoring guide that it caught on some runs and missed on others, and fixed them by making that check mandatory.

### A rubric's rules must fit together

Check that a rubric's rules can all be met at once. With easy items defined as recall and recall-only items failed, 26 of 37 easy items failed cognitive demand.

An AP benchmark's judge context said easy items should test basic recall and comprehension, and also that questions should test historical thinking, not just factual recall. One run's report found items were either too simple and failed cognitive demand or too complex and failed difficulty, and in a later run 26 of 37 easy items failed cognitive demand. After the rule was relaxed to accept recall, the judge's 25-case calibration set still expected a recall-only question to fail cognitive demand.

### A rule nothing checks is a reminder

Record each content rule's scope and what checks it, because a rule nothing checks is only a reminder.

The reading workspace's laws file pairs each law with a check that the pre-commit hook runs, and says a law without a check is not a law but a memory. A plan to centralise the reading standards binds each rule to one or more evidence lanes: deterministic code, a model judge that is advisory until calibrated, the live student or runtime surface, and expert human review. A rule-by-rule audit found rules whose enforcement notes scoped them far narrower than they read, and recommended a consistent scope line on each.

### A target success rate per question

Give each question a target success rate and treat a result far from it, either way, as a fault in the question. One design targets about 100% success on its first closing question and about 80% on its second.

The closing-questions design sets a success gradient of about 100% for naming the idea, about 80% for finding it in the text and no key for using it: if children fail the first it is built wrong, and if nearly everyone aces the second it is too easy to be worth asking (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). It grounds the gradient in a high success rate in guided practice, which it rates well evidenced and attributes to Rosenshine.

### A wrong fact is never polish

A wrong fact in the text, the key or any line a student reads is never a polish note: it holds the item back until fixed. Of 24 minor findings in one review, the 4 lines untrue to the story were fixed and the rest left as polish.

A Grade 3 demonstration unit sends every world claim in its passages to an independent factuality pass: any failed or unresolved claim holds the text as a draft, and a wrong world claim in a child's science text is a kill, not a footnote. A later review register of four lessons acted on minor findings only when a line was untrue to the story, folding those into the fix batch, and listed a find-it key that taught a fact not in the story among its serious fixes. A wrong fact holds the item back however good the rest of it is, and it is never a footnote either.

Quoted:

### Account for every point of feedback

Map every point of feedback on its own to a decision and its evidence, and never drop one or bury it in a bulk statement that feedback was addressed.

The standard's golden checklist asks whether every point raised in review is individually accounted for: each source point needs a disposition and links to one or more requirements and exact evidence, so that nothing material is lost behind a bulk statement that feedback was addressed (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, Q002). The 1.0 standard names bulk 'addressed' claims, missing source points and evidence with no feedback link as its failure signals (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`), and the base red-team profile maps each point to criteria and evidence and says feedback is neither dropped nor silently promoted into universal policy (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/standards/student-course-quality/profiles/base/RED_TEAM_BASE.source.json`).

### Add up the headroom first

Before committing to an overall target, add up each item type's realistic headroom to see whether the target can be reached and which type decides it. With every other type near its ceiling, the weakest type at its best-ever rate gave 83.8% overall against a 95% target.

Per-type arithmetic on measured pass rates was written into the project's target file as something to read before approving any spend (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md`). A 95% target meant 282 of 297 prompts passing; with every other type near its estimated ceiling, the weakest type at its best-ever rate gave 249 of 297 (83.8%), and at an 80% pass rate 276 of 297 (92.9%). That made the weakest type the binding constraint.

Quoted:

- `icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md` (19): “Operationally: **282 of 297 prompts must pass.**”
- `icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md` (44): “**Without solving DBQ:** non-DBQ ceilings at +47, DBQ at all-time-best +11 = **+58 max**. 191 + 58 = **249/297 = 83.8%.** Below bar.”
- `icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md` (46): “**With DBQ at 80% pass rate (24+24=48 vs current 10):** +38 from DBQ + +47 from non-DBQ = +85. **191 + 85 = 276/297 = 92.9%.** Still below bar.”
- `icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/mission_locked_95_aggregate.md` (52): “DBQ is the structural constraint.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-final-selection/_internal/VERDICT.md` (39): “**The strict variety cap (match ≤6/15) is unreachable regardless of Claude** — a structural non-match shortage (623 available vs 729 needed), not a wiring bug.”

### An instruction is not a guard

Telling an agent not to change content doesn't stop it: hash content files before and after automated work, and keep every change as an edit that can be replayed. An agent told never to edit a lesson file overwrote it from a stale copy, caught only because a test's count came out 186 instead of 187.

During a fan-out of model agents in the reading project, one agent left the lesson file at a stale snapshot and four content edits vanished, despite an explicit prompt clause never to edit that file; it was caught only because a test's count pin came out 186 instead of 187 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd`). The root cause it records is that a prompt instruction is not a write guard, since an agent's shell can write wherever the main loop can; the fix is to hash every content file before a fan-out, check it when each agent returns, treat any change as an incident, and keep every content change as an operations file so re-applying it is one command (the same file).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd` (145-148): “left the working file at a 21:15 snapshot — four content ops (tappability spans, a decoy line) vanished — despite an explicit prompt clause "never edit public/lesson-json/grade-3.json." Caught only because `semantic-coverage.test.mjs`'s count pin moved (186 ≠ 187).”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd` (149): “**Root cause:** a prompt instruction is not a write guard — a fan-out's Bash has the same filesystem”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0199-engineering-git-gate-traps.qmd` (152-155): “before any fan-out that touches harnesses/tests, record `md5 -q public/lesson-json/grade-3.json` (and any other content file); re-check it when every agent returns and treat any change as an incident (re-apply from saved ops files, never hand-patch). Keep every content mutation as an ops file under the batch record (`apply-ops.py`) so re-application is one idempotent command.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/round-2/independent-review-by-unit1.md` (41): “I compared the entire current U9 Lesson7 parsed object with baseline da0b0b42 after excluding only that new node. **They are equal.**”

- `othello-archive/scripts/build_content.py` (12): “--check  rebuilds in memory and fails if the committed JSON differs or any quote is not verbatim.”

### An objection stands until withdrawn

In a review panel, an evidence-backed objection stands until whoever raised it withdraws it after a traced repair, and no vote settles a question of fact.

A design for an adversarial review panel of AI agents treats silence as missing work, never assent, and lets a valid evidence-backed block stand until whoever raised it withdraws it after a traced repair. Its charter lets the panel adopt rules and plans but not vote facts into existence or grant approvals, which stay with named authorities. An audit of the build found remand passing generic error strings instead of the original blocking ballot and its evidence, and replacement ballots evaluated without the blocker withdrawing. The audit's scope notes conclude that a ten-agent vote cannot turn missing runtime evidence or missing human approval into fact.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/adversarial-course-council/AGENTS.md` (17): “9. Silence is missing work, never assent. A valid evidence-backed block survives until its author withdraws it after a traced repair.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/adversarial-course-council/CHARTER.md` (41): “The council may adopt a rule, implementation plan, critique disposition, or bounded course-design decision. It may not vote facts into existence or grant academic approval, source rights, item certification, live runtime proof, deployment, regulatory compliance, or student outcomes. Those remain with their named authorities.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/council-human-handover-2026-08-13/03_AUDIT_FINDINGS_AND_OPEN_RISKS.md` (51): “Remand passed generic error strings rather than the original blocking ballot, author, evidence, challenged clauses, and ballot digest. Replacement ballots were evaluated without requiring the blocker to explicitly withdraw after a traced repair.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/council-human-handover-2026-08-13/01_SCOPE_AND_TIMELINE.md` (58): “- A ten-agent vote cannot convert missing runtime evidence or missing human approval into fact.”

Against: The panel never ran and was retired: '- Live model work: **never started**.' A rule elsewhere accepts that an objection may be overruled and asks only that it be logged with its reasoning and rechecked in the next round.

### Authored is not delivered

Judge content by what the delivered player shows, checking files, the student's live experience and course claims apart, and count an authored element or gate only once seen working. One course build's feedback was silent, 0/542, and two live courses had a null mastery threshold, so their 90% gate didn't block.

A course quality gate failed one course build with its feedback silent, 0/542, and the course checklist now requires the live response check to return the authored feedback, not the generic fallback, because authored is not the same as resolves. The renderer's notes add that content without proper response processing shows no feedback at all in strict mode. An evaluation of one live course found its 90% mastery threshold declared in metadata but not enforced by any observable mechanism, and a merge found the threshold null on both live courses, so the 90% gate didn't block; the course-fix skill now says to prove a gate with a play-through rather than assert a metadata field as enforced. Check in code that every authored element reaches a surface the student uses, count anything never shown as missing, and count a gate as working only once it is seen blocking.

### Beat what the records already predict

Before a new test takes learners' time, measure the error of the cheapest existing alternative, such as predicting from records already held, and show the test beats it head-to-head. An adversarial review cited a model built from learners' records as already predicting the official score with a mean absolute error of 7.28, and the new test's case never compared itself with it.

A red team on an interim reading assessment found that its case for spending student time never named an existing prediction model built from learners' records, never compared itself with it and never explained why direct measurement beats that prediction at no extra student time; the model's write-up measured a mean absolute error of 7.28 against the official test (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md`, line 33). The recheck found the head-to-head committed in advance, with its baseline leg running before any student time was spent (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RECHECK_FINDINGS.md`, line 7). The baseline costs learners nothing, so a test earns its minutes only by beating it.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/RED_TEAM_FINDINGS.md` (33): “the package **never names it, compares against it, or explains why direct measurement beats prediction-from-existing-signals at zero additional student time.**”

No writeup of the cited model could be found: a search "finds **no writeup of any RIT-prediction model with MAE 7.28 / RMSE 9.53**" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/red-team/PROTEST_BRIEF.md`, line 47). The package accepts that the comparison could stop the project: "If the retrospective readout shows prediction already meets the need, that is a legitimate reason to stop — we are asking for the comparison, not assuming its outcome." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_CASE_FOR_APPROVAL.md`, line 154). The readout had not yet run; it waited on access to the reporting data.

### Bind each check to what it checked

Tie every check's result to the digest of the build and screen it checked, so a relevant change withdraws the result and reruns the affected checks. A package downloaded earlier matched 0 of 55 current lesson digests.

The reading course's quality gates hold one pinned build per round, because changes landing on the main branch mid-round invalidated in-progress rounds three times (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/key-quality-gates.md`, lines 148-149). Its quality standard makes every evidence record carry artifact and dependency digests, so that a relevant change forces the affected checks to rerun (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/standards/student-course-quality/versions/2.0.0/GOLDEN-CHECKLIST.qmd`, line 35). A package downloaded earlier matched 0 of 55 lesson digests and 0 of 7 showcase digests in the current build, and was barred from reuse as a source. Review one frozen, pinned build at a time, and compare versions only on the same base.

### Blind, shuffled and double-scored review

Score compared versions blind to which system or maker produced each, in shuffled order, and have a second person independently score a preset share plus every disputed or severe case. One plan has a second person independently score a preset 25% of the first reviews, 168 of them, plus every disputed or severe case.

An experiment plan hides model identities and response order from the people scoring, and has a second person independently score a preset, stratified 25% of the first reviews (168) plus every disputed or severe case, with differences adjudicated (`uae-education-ai/HERETIC_PLAN.md`). Its harness treats the first-review report as preliminary until those second reviews and the dispute coverage exist (`uae-education-ai/HARNESS.md`). Keep tuning and calibration items out of the final evaluation.

### Block unsupported scores in code

Enforce in code the limits on what a score may claim, so no unvalidated score or prediction of a real test appears until evidence supports it. Two audits found a figure drifting between documents, 0.930 in one and 0.928 in another.

The case for approval of a pre-pilot proxy for an outside reading test enforces its claims ladder in code: before a pilot the engine returns only a logit with its standard error and domain sub-scores, and the RIT, percentile and CGP scales are blocked, so a score report cannot be misread into a claim the number would carry, because the number is not in the response (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5_build_2026_07_02/mapproxy_clean.md`). It gives the reason that two audits had found number drift in its documents, 0.930 against 0.928, so the gate that carries the claim lives in code, not prose. The limits cover any score on an outside test's scale, and the evidence that lifts them can be a linking study of the same students taking both tests close together.

### Break results down before fixing

Before choosing a fix or calling a change a gain, break results down by item type, unit and failure kind, and apply changes only where they help: averages hide losses. One gate abandoned a change if any key item type fell 5 points or more, however the overall score moved.

A synthesis across five corpora of the AP work makes dimension-aware debugging a first-tier rule: every failed result maps to a failed dimension and item type before any fix is chosen, because jumping from an aggregate score to retraining had wasted days and each item type failed for its own reasons (`MASTER_SYNTHESIS.md`, lines 264, 280 and 281). One step-function gate compared each critical item type with its baseline and marked a change dead if any fell by 5 points or more, even when the overall score held (the step-function gate's `source_report.md`, lines 51 and 58). Size each fix by its criterion's share of your own failures, and stop on a collapse in any one item type.

Supplying the real source documents themselves helped the document-based type (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/STATE_CURRENT_2026_05_12T0805Z.md`, line 88), so the rule is about added background facts, not the source texts.

### Bring back every must-learn item

Check that every item marked must-learn comes back for retrieval from memory in a later lesson, since a unit plan can leave whole lessons' must-learn items never recalled. In one unit, only one of the three lessons whose retrieval recalls the previous lesson asks for a key line from memory.

A design note for a 3D version audited the unit's knowledge base and found that of the three lessons whose retrieval recalls the previous lesson, only one asks for a key line from memory, so the must-learn lines of two lessons are never brought back from memory and by the last lesson's closing tasks students must find quotes again rather than recall them. The knowledge base's retrieval column holds a single quote-analysis row for the unit. The note calls retrieval of exact wording the one thing a closing essay needs and the knowledge base leaves to chance.

Quoted:

- `othello-archive/design-notes/spaced-quote-recall.md` (8): “have no quote row. So the red (store-cupboard) lines from L2 and L3 are never brought back from memory, and by the”
- `othello-archive/design-notes/spaced-quote-recall.md` (24): “Retrieval practice of exact wording is the one thing a closing essay needs and the KB leaves to chance.”
- `othello-archive/sources/act1/KB - Knowledge Base.csv` (99): “Quote analysis: What did ""I follow him to serve my turn upon him.”

Against: The fix it proposes, one finish-the-line row in each later lesson's retrieval, was never built (`othello-archive/design-notes/spaced-quote-recall.md`, line 3, "Status: proposal only. Nothing built.").

### Build and check against released exams

Build and check generated items and marking guides against the exam's official released items, scoring guidelines and scored sample answers wherever they exist.

The research survey in the AP question work found no academic benchmark for this kind of question generation, and named the exam body's released past exams, with complete scoring guidelines, evidence examples and sample student responses, as the only verified items and guides (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`). It called them the ground-truth rubrics a training set should be derived from or validated against. This is a recommendation: the project's checks did not yet use them.

These are the ground-truth rubrics that a fine-tuning dataset should be derived from or validated against.”

The College Board materials are the only source of verified AP-style questions and rubrics. ### Change the format, never the content

When a delivery format or schema cannot carry approved content, change the format, the schema or the code that renders it, never the content's claims, sources or meaning. A plan for a 130-lesson course aborts any step that would change authored historical meaning to fit delivery.

A production plan for moving an authored 130-session AP history course into a delivery contract says a failed slice repairs the projector or contract, never the historical claim merely to satisfy presentation. Its gates abort any step that would change historical content, fabricate evidence, or change authored meaning, source binding or assessment candidates. The course's status file reports the contract binding all 130 lessons, with one projection passing deterministic and leakage checks. It widens the media rule of meeting a length limit by splitting material rather than cutting approved words.

### Check against something that doesn't assume the answer

Check what a machine made against something that doesn't assume the answer. A transcriber given the script passed takes that began with extra speech; one given nothing caught all four.

Finding 6 and "What kept going wrong" in the film study (`othello-unit-video/research/FINDINGS.md`): a voice model read
its style instructions aloud at the start of all four takes. A transcriber given the script passed them; one not given
it caught one; Whisper, run with no prompt, caught all four. A fidelity score built on a recogniser's transcript put a
word-perfect film at 98.4% (`othello-unit-video/.claude/skills/uvk-video-compare/SKILL.md`), and a frame check that
matched file names passed a repaint whose picture had changed.

### Check cited results against their sources

Before acting on a cited result, requirement or analysis of what a test measures, check it against its original source, because summaries merge, move and relabel what they cite. A 13.83% gain in citation grounding was later cited as a "13-50% grounding improvement".

Comparing the AP question work's summaries with the sections they summarise turned up several drifts. A 13.83% gain in citation grounding, with only about half the sentences fully covered (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_rag_factual_grounding.md`), became an expected "13-50% grounding improvement" in the same summary and "Published results" in the strategy note (`icloud-work/ML learnings/master_strategy_apr24.md`). A 96% validity result belongs to custom-chunked retrieval in one study, but the index credits it to graph retrieval (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_educational_content_generation.md`, `icloud-work/ML learnings/INDEX.md`). An internal team result was called published, and a verification method's result was cited for a pre-writing step it never tested (`icloud-work/ML learnings/research_qwen3_structured_multistage.md`). For a requirement, the source to check against is the official one.

However, only ~50% of sentences achieved perfect citation coverage without fine-tuning, suggesting a ceiling that requires SFT to overcome fully.”

### Check every part and every version

Check every line a student reads, passages, options, keys, definitions and every rewrite, for the subject's known misconceptions, flagging hits in code before publication whoever wrote it. In one unit, the lesson sweeps found a misconception outside the passage three times: in a keyed answer, a check option and a taught word's definition.

A science synthesis asks for its absolute prohibitions, such as saying energy is used up, to be automated checks on any content made for the curriculum, whether by people or AI (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Cross-Cutting Synthesis.docx`), and the coherence guidance sends all science-related text through the misconception check (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Brainlift social science and science coherence.md`). In one unit, the lesson sweeps changed a keyed answer from plants making energy from sunlight to plants making food (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.2 - The Living World - Lesson Designs/3.2 - 1. The Wonderful World of Plants - FIND - Lesson Design (v2 - MCQ pauses + science sweep).docx`), reworded a check option and redefined a taught word, while other sweeps found nothing to fix. A comparison made in this run found a draft science text and its rewrite byte-identical, both still saying the rest of the energy is lost as heat or used up (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/G4 DRAFT/Rewrites/2. Ecosystems and Food Webs - rewrite.docx`). The check covers phrasing known to teach a misconception as well as the misconception itself.

### Check every promise a task makes

Where a task promises all of something or a range, check that every member is there.

A content-integrity check written for the course plans expands ranges and words such as all or every into canonical IDs, treats them as exhaustive, and compares the promised lessons, entities, operations, sources, chart rows, tasks and rubric categories with what is actually present (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/skills/course-content-integrity/SKILL.md`). It requires chart and rubric closure, so anything shown as valid is accepted consistently, and it fails missing entities, omitted operations, inconsistent row logic and a rubric that rejects its own chart (the same file).

### Check how people are portrayed

Review generated text and pictures for stereotyped or insensitive portrayals of people.

Line-level review of a generated article flagged a sentence that singled out a group's performance skills as repeating a bias the group still faces, and asked for it to be rephrased (`icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/ap_files/Articles Tracker.xlsx`, sheet 'Sheet9', cell C15). Review of another article flagged a generated illustration of a slave ship with people on it as likely to be seen as insensitive, and asked for a more symbolic image or another subject from the topic (sheet 'APUSH Articles', cell M12). Show an atrocity through a symbolic image or another part of the topic, not a generated realistic scene with people in it.

Quoted:

- `icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/ap_files/Articles Tracker.xlsx` (sheet 'Sheet9', cell C15): “The focus on musical rhythms and ways of performing alongside farming skills, while not incorrect, suggests that their performance skills made them stand out. Please rephrase this, as this is a bias that African Americans still face today, limiting roles and spheres of influence.”
- `icloud-work/k_12_social_studies/ap_files/Articles Tracker.xlsx` (sheet 'APUSH Articles', cell M12): “I don't think we should illustrate a slave ship using AI, at least not with people on it. It could be considered by many to be insensitive. I would create an alternate image that's more symbolic or has to do with something else in the topic.”

Against: Only two instances were recorded and no systematic check existed, so how often this happens is unknown.

### Check obligations as well as prohibitions

Check what an output must contain as well as what it must avoid, so an empty or minimal output that breaks no rule still fails.

The pedagogy decision-bank experiment design requires both positive obligations and prohibitions, so an empty or minimal artifact fails completeness even if it avoids every violation. Its headline metric counts only held-out tasks that produce a complete artifact satisfying every active critical rule, which keeps an output from passing by doing nothing.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0131-pedagogy-decision-bank-experiment-intake.qmd` (405-406): “Positive obligations and prohibitions are both required; an empty/minimal artifact fails completeness even if it avoids violations.”

### Check the design against its target

When review rounds settle into cosmetic findings, check the design against the target it claims to serve, because quiet rounds can hide a real gap. Three rounds of cosmetic findings hid that a writing plan's knowledge-component spine covered only one of the three constructed-response types its target test uses.

Three red-team rounds on a grade 4–5 writing plan converged on naming, counts and cross-references; the fourth deliberately widened the aperture and checked the plan against the test blueprint it claimed to target (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R4.md`). It found that the plan's knowledge-component spine covered only one of the blueprint's three constructed-response types, a gap the package never stated. The gap was then disclosed and mapped rather than rebuilt.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R4.md` (12-14): “The convergence to > cosmetics in R1–R3 was masking that nobody had checked the plan against the blueprint it claims to > target — R4 did, and found a gap.”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R4.md` (27): “The package targets the STAAR CR blueprint but its KC spine covers only ONE of its three CR types”

Against: The project's review gauntlet ends each layer once it goes dry, at "two consecutive rounds with zero new findings" (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/train-teacher-requirements.md`, lines 164-165), so convergence alone would end a review.

### Check the scope labels first

Check every scope label against the official framework before an item is made or judged, pass it explicitly and unchanged through every step, and confirm how the judge reads it. One wrong period mapping in a generator's settings caused 77 curriculum-alignment hard-fails, the majority of all failures in its baseline.

In one quality push on an AP question generator, its settings mapped several units to the wrong period, so items matched their topic but carried the wrong time period, and the evaluator hard-failed them on curriculum alignment (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark/CHANGELOG_RELENTLESS.md`). That single settings error caused 77 hard-fails in the baseline, the majority of all failures. The evaluator in turn returned systematically wrong unit numbers for one course's standards, so the generator corrected them before evaluation (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/CHANGELOG.md`). The labels are the course, unit, period, standard and procedure. Match them to the framework by content, and pass them along as given.

### Check what a cut takes away

Before cutting or trimming part of a lesson, check what only it supplies and what later lessons ask of it. One audit found a later unit's two transfer questions pointing at exactly the two ideas the served lessons failed to land.

A curriculum adherence audit (`grade3-reading/artifacts/curriculum-adherence-2026-09-24/REPORT.md`, 2026-09-24) compared four served lessons with their designs and with a later unit's transfer questions. One lesson had halved its key idea, that a setting sets the rules and the mood, to mood alone, while the later unit asks where else the child has seen a setting set the rules and the mood; two of that unit's transfer questions point at exactly the two ideas two of the lessons fail to land. The same audit found that cutting an added word routine the design forbids would leave the child with no old-London background at all, because the film meant to carry it did not and the knowledge page designed for it was absent. A halved idea leaves a later question pointing at something the learner never met.

### Check what an item demands, not its tag

Check, item by item rather than from tags or averages, that each item and lesson actually demands the skill, standard, topic and passage its labels claim. One grade 3 course needed 193 items retagged for systematic mistags.

One grade 3 reading course had systematic standard mistags, vocabulary in context on the wrong standard and comprehension on the wrong strand, and 193 items were retagged; the generator's rubric now audits tags and reports an error rate (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/course-formula-agents.md`). After a retag counted as successful, a main-idea lesson still served an inference item, so the check is the skill claimed against the skill assessed, item by item (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`), and the course-plan standard calls such a lesson a tagging and a teaching defect (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/instruction-quality-standard.md`). Tag coverage is plumbing, never the curriculum claim (the same file), and the grade 3 criteria ask that every standard map to at least one knowledge component, with no orphans and no false alignment, where an item matches a standard's vocabulary but its depth of knowledge is lower (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D7-knowledge-first-curriculum.md`). Make the item-by-item check a blocking check of its own. Where a lesson's items do not demand the skill it claims to teach, fix the content rather than the tag, since a retagged item can fit its new tag and still break the lesson.

### Check what shared code assumes

When content or code is shared or ported between courses or levels, compare their conventions one by one and check what the shared code assumes. A new level's word cards dropped a say-the-word step on 28 of 28 cards that the shipped level used on 12 of 12.

A review that compared every convention of a new level's lessons with the level already shipped found that the new level's word cards silently dropped the say-the-word step, 28 of 28 cards against 12 of 12 (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R5.md`). A later review found a marking prompt that serves every grade hard-coding "a sentence a third grader could say aloud" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-09-15-R22.md`), and a port of display code assumed a field the new course never had, so its fallback silently produced a worse screen instead of failing loudly (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-21-R8.md`). Otherwise silent departures and wording fixed to one level slip through.

### Choose core content by consensus

Choose core content by how many independent sources include it, with a fixed inclusion threshold. One social studies set drew on 16,345 standards from 51 jurisdictions and kept only content at its moderate threshold or above.

A consensus social studies standards workbook records its method: consensus thresholds (CORE 38+, HIGH 26-37, MODERATE 13-25, LOW <13) over standards drawn from 51 jurisdictions, a resolution principle that favours knowledge-rich, recently revised standards where its backbone states conflict, and a note that a skills-only framework carries no content mandates (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx`, sheet 'Methodology Notes'). Its first tab includes only standards at MODERATE or above. It is a method; no outcome was measured. Settle conflicts in favour of the knowledge-rich, recently revised source, and do not rely on a skills-only framework alone.
