### Keep student-facing lines out of the player

Keep every line a student sees in the lesson's data, not the player: a line built into a player for one text can show up wrongly on other texts.

Exporting the Grade 9 lesson engine's lessons into two other players turned up lines written into those players for their own text (`g9-transformer-audit/2026-10-09-builders.json`). In an animated version the mimicry step always gives the same reply and its speech hints name one play's cast, the sentence-rebuild nudge is keyed by option text, so options such as 'noun' or 'adverb' get a nudge about one word on any text, and one character's name is printed beside every quote. In a 3D version a card label is shared, so the engine sends its web links only when the web's centre is the word that label names, and it patches other fixed strings, such as an act and scene, for texts that have none (`g9/transformer/src/glue/threejs-render.js`). The players were read-only to the engine, so its export could work around these limits but not fix them.

### Lesson counts are forecasts to test

Treat a course's lesson counts as forecasts to test on a timed pilot unit, and when the material needs more time, re-plan the calendar rather than cut content or teaching. One plan forecast 130 teaching sessions and left the rest of the framework's suggested periods for assessment, review and remediation.

An AP history course plan forecast 130 teaching sessions against the framework's 140 suggested class periods, reserving the difference for assessments, cumulative review, remediation and final exam practice, and made its first unit the pacing pilot. Its rule is that the counts are assumptions to test: measured time on that unit triggers a whole-course reforecast, and the plan never keeps a neat count by removing difficult content, shortening source work or treating assessment as instruction. If the estimate grows, the calendar changes or only genuinely co-dependent topics are combined.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz` (apush/docs/BRAINLIFT.md inside it) (524-526): “The proposed lesson counts are assumptions to test. If Unit 1 requires more time for source access, writing, or correction, the whole-course forecast changes. The plan does not preserve a neat count by removing difficult content, shortening source work, or treating assessment as instruction.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz` (apush/docs/SEQUENCING-BRIEF.md inside it) (122-123): “If the estimate grows, adjust the calendar or combine only genuinely co-dependent topics. Never delete a KC, replace teaching with an item set, or compress a source-analysis handoff into an answer reveal.”

### List every line not in the source

Generate from the content itself a list of every learner-facing line that is not word for word from the approved source, so each can be approved, rewritten or cut. One such generated list held 480 of a 3D version's own student-facing lines.

A 3D version keeps its approved source's words verbatim and writes, from its own code, a file of every student-facing sentence that is not word for word from the source, grouped by file, so the builders' lines can be approved or rewritten in one pass; the file says it is generated and must not be edited by hand, and it counts 480 lines. A separate fidelity gate fails any quoted run of two or more words in the code that does not appear in the sources.

### Log overruled objections and recheck them

Record every review objection that was overruled, with its reasoning, and check it again in the next round, so a recurrence counts as evidence rather than memory. An objection overruled on 08-06 was raised independently by a later review on 08-11.

The red-team skill for the reading course plans makes this its rule 14 and gives the case behind it: on 08-06 the team argued that a pre-filled quote inverts the release gradient, was told to implement it without pushback, and on 08-11 a later review raised the same point independently (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`). Without the log the earlier objection is only a memory; with it, it is calibration evidence for the next disagreement.

### Log what learners did, not inferences

Log what learners did as raw events and compute any model's reading of them later, so the record doesn't change when the model does.

The reading project's item-level telemetry schema was written before any pilot, so that outcome data would exist from the first day, and it stores no inference fields such as predicted mastery, a risk score or an engagement index, which are analysis on top of the raw events (`grade3-reading/artifacts/cert-layer/TELEMETRY-SCHEMA-v0-2026-08-31.md`). Its reason is that a model's opinion baked into the log would make the log disagree with itself the day the model changes, while an append-only raw log never has to be collected again when the analysis improves (the same file).

### Machine checks are not judgment

Keep machine checks apart from human judgment: a quality call stays unjudged until a person has watched or listened, and an AI judge only picks what that person reviews.

Every number in the first film's QA comes from a measurement on the delivered files, and none replaces a real
audition (`g9-film-v01-render/QA.md`); a review marked a quality call "present, unjudged" where it needed a listen
(`g9/review/2026-10-06-film-reviews/VIDEO-REVIEW.md`); and a successful render is technical proof only
(`g9/tools/unit-video-essay/INTEGRATION.md`). AI judges are a filter: a voice is chosen by listening
(`othello-unit-video/research/METHODS.md`), and automated player runs are muted, so a person still has to watch with
sound (`othello-unit-video/.claude/skills/uvk-checks-make/SKILL.md`).

### Make a review loop converge

In a repeated review loop, act only on findings that show harm rather than preference, keep earlier decisions unless new evidence arrives, and pause after a round with nothing critical.

The reading project's quality rules name oscillation as the failure mode of an unsupervised improve-loop, each round fixing what the round before chose. So a finding must prove harm, not preference; recorded decisions are immutable inside the loop, and a later round may escalate a deferred item only with new evidence; and a round with zero critical findings pauses the loop. Its change-control baseline adds that recency, confidence and citation count do not supersede an earlier decision and holds a change of direction for one consolidated decision, and a later review brief downgrades a pattern already in the signed baseline to a note unless it actively harms the child.

### Make the changes, then walk once

Make the changes and run the quicker checks before one full walk-through of a lesson, rather than walking, failing, patching and walking again. The rule came after two cycles of walking, failing and patching were stopped.

In a rebuild of a reading lesson, a "changes-first, then one walk" discipline started formally at tick 30, after two walk-fail-patch-walk cycles (journeys 32 and 33) were stopped: from then on a fan-out of the driver lens and the verifiers ran before the single walk (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0222-g3-l4-l1-parity-rebuild-2026-09-17-to-21.qmd`). The walks are runs of a Playwright-based walker (the same file).

### Map the misconceptions before teaching

Before teaching a concept, write down its end-of-course target, each known misconception with its persistence, cost and origin, when each framework teaches it, and the riskiest points in the sequence.

The science misconception guidance in the curriculum folder gives each concept a card with the same parts: the target students must ultimately reach, a map of each misconception rated by persistence and impact with its origin, a trace of when and how each framework teaches the concept, and the highest-risk points in the teaching sequence (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Chemistry Misconception Prevention Guidance.docx`, lines 6-9). In the maps, impact is what a misconception costs on the AP exam and origin is where it comes from, such as textbooks, everyday language or documentaries (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Biology Misconception Prevention Guidance.docx`, lines 9-18). The guides rank concepts on different grounds, biology by exam weight and chemistry by how foundational a concept is, so no ranking rule is claimed (Biology line 5, Chemistry line 15).

### Match curriculum data by content

Find and match curriculum data, lesson parts and source texts by their content and structure, never by identifiers or titles, which drift or shift wholesale. 224 of 239 local entries for one course matched the canonical source by content, but 218 of those sat at a different identifier.

When the AP work's evaluator reconciled its history curriculum data with the canonical curriculum repository, one course's local entries turned out to be systematically off by one period: 224 of 239 had a strong content match, but 218 of those were at a different identifier (commit fb17482 in `icloud-work/inceptbench`). The merge rebuilt that course on the canonical identifiers, carried the local content onto each record by a Jaccard match, kept the old identifier on every remapped record, and carried over the 16 entries with no match unchanged.

### Measure a conversation by turns and uptake

Measure a comprehension conversation by the turns it runs, how much language the learner produces and whether each reply used the learner's answer, not by responses per minute alone. One blueprint treats about five turns as the shape of a comprehension conversation.

The opportunities-to-respond BrainLift's blueprint measures with three signals, not one: responses per minute, turns per conversation and how much language the child produces, along with whether the app actually used the child's answer (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md`, line 106). Following the Strive-for-Five model it treats about five turns as the shape of a comprehension conversation (line 84), and a reply that would read the same whatever the child answered is not a third turn (line 86). Which measures to build, and how to capture young children's spoken answers well enough to score them, it leaves open (line 192).

Quoted:

- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md` (106): “Measure with three signals, not one: responses per minute, turns per conversation, and how much language the child produces, along with whether the app actually used the child’s answer.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md` (84): “the app should treat about five turns as the shape of a comprehension conversation”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md` (86): “A reply that would read the same no matter what the child answered is not a third turn.”
- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/pedagogy/otr-brainlift-2026-07-24.md` (192): “The open questions to work through are which of these measures to build into the app, and how to capture a young child’s spoken responses reliably enough to score them.”

Published: [Cabell & Zucker 2024, Using Strive-for-Five conversations to strengthen language comprehension in preschool through Grade One, The Reading Teacher](https://doi.org/10.1002/trtr.2266)

Against: The BrainLift was written for PreK to Grade 2 and calls itself out of scope for grades 3 and above; the Grade 3 course that adopted it treats its age-band specifics as context only (the same file, line 12).

<sub>method · stage: measure · measurement, evidence-of-learning · universal · from g3, research · adopted-rule · held · found in [2026-10-12-5-full-crawl](../research/2026-10-12-5-full-crawl/)</sub>

### Measure early readers' rate, not only accuracy

For early readers, measure oral reading rate as well as accuracy, since rate tracks standardized reading scores more closely, and a reader can be accurate yet slow. In one grade-2 cohort of 51 learners, words correct per minute correlated 0.43 with the standardized reading percentile, against 0.20 for accuracy.

A proxy check on 51 second-grade learners with at least five fluency attempts and a standardized reading score correlated each fluency measure with the external percentile: words correct per minute at r = 0.43, accuracy at r = 0.20 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md`, lines 58-64). A pedagogy red team on the same course had argued that accuracy is the least sensitive fluency measure, that rate and prosody are what predict comprehension, and that a cohort can be 86% accurate and still read slowly, word by word (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-2-pedagogy.md`, line 62).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md` (58): “was run on the 51 G2 students with both ≥5 fluency attempts and a MAP record:”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md` (62): “| Fluency **WCPM** → MAP percentile | **0.43** (moderate) |”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md` (64): “| Fluency **accuracy** → MAP percentile | 0.20 (weak) |”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-2-pedagogy.md` (62): “Accuracy is the *least* sensitive fluency measure; the fluency constructs that actually predict comprehension are **rate (WCPM) and prosody**”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/redteam-2-pedagogy.md` (62): “A cohort can be 86% accurate and still dysfluent (slow, word-by-word, no prosody) — and dysfluent readers comprehend poorly *even when accurate*.”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md` (73): “Caveats: n=51 (only ⅓ of fluency students had a joinable MAP record)”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd` (469): “It was largest (.55) when the outcome measure was word recognition, next largest (.44) with a fluency measure, and smallest (.35) with a comprehension outcome measure.”

Published: [Reading for Understanding: Toward an R&D Program in Reading Comprehension (RAND, 2002)](https://www.rand.org/pubs/monograph_reports/MR1465.html)

Against: Only a third of the fluency learners had a score that could be joined, hence n = 51 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/optionB-prime-narrow-rebuild.md`, line 73). Fluency practice also transfers only moderately: in a meta-analysis of repeated reading, the effect was smallest, .35, on comprehension outcomes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`, line 469).

### Measure the content, not its container

Check that the content itself is in view, the first real passage paragraph and the settled feedback with its next action, by measuring those nodes, never a wrapper.

In a Grade 5 click-through the passage could begin below the visible reading viewport, and correction feedback with its next action could settle outside it (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/G5_STUDENT_EXPERIENCE_RELEASE_GATE.qmd`, lines 26-27). The layout checks had measured containers instead of the first real passage paragraph and had not bound feedback text to its current action (lines 63-64). The release gate now measures the first real passage paragraph, with rendered text geometry and no horizontal overflow, treats a wrapper as insufficient evidence, and requires the response feedback and its current action to be present and fully inside the viewport after each attempt settles, at mobile and desktop sizes (lines 76, 82 and 85).

### Never bend content to pass a check

Never alter an item, request or check just to raise a score: a gain from removing what a check inspects is gaming, so fix the item or harden the check. An edit that disabled detection cut the findings from 28/12 to 15/8, a mix of real cleanup and switched-off checks.

An audit of a Grade 5 course found that an uncommitted lint edit cut findings by weakening the gate: it replaced the total invariant with a condition that is always false, suppressed unit-split failures and broadened exemptions, so the drop from 28/12 to 15/8 was a mix of real cleanup and disabled detection that could not count as progress toward approval (`grade3-reading/artifacts/takeover-audit-2026-07-13/g5-clean-baseline.md`). An earlier fix had inserted a taught word into another lesson's closing page to pass a vocabulary check, and was reverted as editing someone else's lesson to satisfy the validator (`grade3-reading/artifacts/DECISIONS-2026-08-24.md`). A capstone lesson was named by the procedure its thinking fits, read from the procedures' definitions, because the nearest-sounding label would have been mislabelling to satisfy a validator (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/CAPSTONE-PROCEDURE-RULING-2026-08-18.md`), and a later review adjudicated 2-1 that another lesson's procedure label was wrong for a trace that related nothing, fixed by a one-line relabel (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-25-R10.md`). Fix content that fails a sound check rather than loosen the check, judge an expected-answer change by what it does for learners, and confirm that a fix that raises a score improved the item rather than dodged the check.

### No exemption without a cost

An exemption from a check is granted by someone other than whoever claims it, never self-declared, and must put a measured outcome in place of each one it waives.

A self-audit of the reading project's quality gate found a latent escape: any course could declare itself engagement-primary in its README and mark every outcome row not applicable; its proposed fix makes the exemption granted rather than self-declared, with a measured engagement outcome replacing each row it nullifies, so it costs an outcome instead of waiving one (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0069-self-audit-insights.qmd`). A draft certification standard keeps a known-debt list that can only shrink and is never padded to pass a build (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0217-team-direction-2026-09-09.qmd`).

### No override clears a factual failure

Let a recorded human override settle a judgement call, but never let it clear a factual, safety or integrity failure.

The student-course quality standard asks whether human decisions are explicit and accountable for every override, exception, acceptance, rejection or source choice, so that human judgment can improve a course without silently rewriting evidence (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/quality/golden-student-course/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd`, lines 161-165). It accepts an override only when the record holds the original result, the final decision, its reason, who decided, a timestamp and the governed artifact, and it bounds every override: human override cannot erase factual, safety or integrity failures (lines 166-168).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/quality/golden-student-course/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd` (168): “Human override cannot erase factual, safety, or integrity failures.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/quality/golden-student-course/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd` (165): “Learner outcome: Human judgment can improve a course without silently rewriting evidence.”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/quality/golden-student-course/versions/1.0.0/STANDARD.qmd` (164): “Applies when: Every override, exception, acceptance, rejection, or source choice.”

Against: none found

### Nothing closes until its check passes

Close a finding only when the check that found it passes on the current build: a commit, claim or run that happens not to reproduce it is not closure. Most of an 11-item fix report failed the next live review, including the original exploit.

In a Grade 3 reading course, one review returned 30 findings, 22 of them criteria already in the course's own standard: the standard was not missing them, the build shipped without running them (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/BUILD-RULES.md`). A later round re-reported nine rules adopted five days earlier, and the rule written to stop that had itself followed the same failure (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/SKILL.md`, rule 10). Fixes failed the same way: most of an 11-item fix report failed the next live review, including the original exploit, and one item was closed by citing a commit (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/skills/course-red-team/references/finding-taxonomy.md`, section H; `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/key-quality-gates.md`). The course's rules now make every catch a machine check in the same cycle, close a finding only by re-running its finder on the current build, and re-verify every earlier fix after each wave of fixes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`). A fix counts as done on the same terms: on the current delivered build, with a quote of what proves it. Before a round closes, every earlier finding and adopted rule is re-run by number and marked open, fixed or moot.

### One change at a time

Test each change alone against an equally informed control on the same fixed items and conditions, differing only in that change, and adopt it only on a net gain.

An AP training chain kept its settings fixed from version to version under an anti-regression rule that only the data changes. To learn whether a block of curriculum context was needed, it trained two versions side by side that differ only in that block: if the version without it does as well, the block is redundant, and if the one with it does better, the block is doing real work. The control runs on the same fixed items and conditions, the request mix and the writer's examples included.

A changed mix can also expose a real defect: the 90.0% run revealed a genuine conflict between a unit's period and a topic (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/docs/IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSALS.md`, line 251), so the drop was informative even though it was not a regression. A design fixed before any run; the file records no result. A fix confirmed on one item proves little beyond it: the lab's own takeaways say targeted repair probes prove the fix for that family, not the whole unit, and warn against row-specific hacks masquerading as generalized repairs. A filter that hurt in the bundle can still help alone: question-set checks measured net-negative when bundled recovered about 6 of 40 candidates on their own (icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/variant-calibration-lab-snapshot/next_live_run_prep.md, line 65).

### One clean slice before the course

Build and fully review one complete, representative slice of lessons, by hand if need be, before automating or making the rest, and make it the template. The plan allowed 48 hours for one audit-clean slice of 6-7 lessons.

The reading project's delivery plan for a Grade 5 course committed to 48 hours for one audit-clean vertical slice of 6-7 lessons before the rest of the course (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/HOTBUCKET.md`, the 2026-07-15 delivery-control entry). Its control rule replaces every earlier estimate at that gate, and a missed gate changes the date, never the quality bar (the same entry). The slice goes through every check before the rest is made.

### One complete run through finish and reload

Test a lesson in one complete learner run from an empty state through its finish, reloading partway and after saving, and check that progress, gates, rewards and saved work survive.

A Grade 5 click-through exposed several failures at once, among them a correct response that appeared to earn no XP and a reading control that looked active without narration having started (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/docs/G5_STUDENT_EXPERIENCE_RELEASE_GATE.qmd`, lines 18-27). Its postmortem found that the checks proved elements existed but not that a learner could see, understand, hear, correct, complete and resume, and that XP, completion, unlock and persistence had been checked in pieces rather than as one stateful journey through completion and reload (lines 29-31 and 68-69). The release gate now fails closed unless one complete run proves lesson completion, the correct preview XP result, next-lesson unlock and the same state after reload, and review-mode navigation must leave that state unchanged (line 87).

### One manual read is a floor

Treat a single manual review as a floor: a second read, blind to the first, finds what the first missed. Four of one review's medium findings came only from the second, blind read.

A merged review of one reading lesson combined two independent manual reads, the second blind to the first. They agreed on every high finding and on most mediums, but each found things the other missed: four mediums came only from the second read, which also caught that a page the first had dismissed on length was hidden. Every finding only one read raised was checked against the lesson file before it went in.

- `shadow-content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md` (286): “The two manual reads agreed on every high and on most mediums, but each found things the other missed. Four of the mediums above … came only from the second read. Treat one manual read as a floor, not a complete review.”

- `othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/process/REVIEW-ROUNDS.md` (10-12): “Links went out on the strength of green validators. ... explicitly asked for two humans reviewing before anything is sent again.”

Against: No counter-evidence found; it rests on one merged review of one lesson.

### Pin the exam specification by date

Pin the official exam specification a course targets by effective date and digest, and re-check every item type and generator schema against it whenever it changes. A legacy short-answer generator still set its stimulus to null, though every short-answer question on the May 2027 exam is sourced.

An audit of an AP history course found that its legacy short-answer generator's schema set the stimulus to null, although every short-answer question on the May 2027 exam is sourced, so its items fit only the old format, and the course then accepted no legacy short-answer item by shape alone. The course's design notes hold that an exam-format change is not only a schema issue: an author who silently uses the prior format makes a whole practice sequence teach the wrong task. Pinning the official authority, effective date, retrieval date and digest is therefore treated as part of instructional quality, and the framework's frozen digest and retrieval date are kept in a source manifest.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz` (apush/docs/BRAINLIFT.md inside it) (301-305): “An exam-format change is not only a schema issue. If all SAQs become sourced, students need repeated instruction in reading different source modalities under short-answer timing. If an author silently uses the prior format, a whole practice sequence teaches the wrong task. Pinning official authority, effective date, retrieval date, and digest is therefore part of instructional quality, not clerical overhead.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz` (apush/docs/CED-LOCAL-RECONCILIATION.md inside it) (46): “The local APUSH SAQ generator schema sets `stimulus` to `null`.”
- `grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz` (apush/docs/CED-LOCAL-RECONCILIATION.md inside it) (46): “No legacy SAQ is accepted by shape alone.”

Against: none found

### Pipeline failures are not content failures

Report a pass rate over every requested item from live verdicts only, keeping errored, unrun or cached checks and other pipeline failures apart from content failures, none dropped. Judge timeouts on long outputs made one item type read 13.3% when its true rate was put at about 45%.

In the AP project, lumping server errors with unreadable outputs produced a false claim that one version was more brittle, and the lesson was to count transport, parse and schema failures separately (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/LESSONS_LEARNED.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/MEMORY.md`). Judge timeouts on long outputs, at about 67% of one type's gradings, made that type read 13.3% when its true rate was put at about 45%, and leaving generation errors out overstated historical pass rates by 10-25 points (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/STATE_CURRENT_2026_05_12T0805Z.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/research/failure_taxonomy.md`). A 0/150 run came from a judge address that pointed at a dead machine, a 6.67-point 'drift' from an output-cleaning pattern that missed the model's tag, and a misnested score lookup silently returned 0.0 (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`; the memory file), so the standing rule is to check the judge's health before diagnosing the model on any all-zero or all-fail result. When the checking tool also fails on the unchanged base, judge the change by the failures it adds.

Quoted:

A clean pipeline audit is weak evidence on its own: one came back 'All three CLEAN;' (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/SESSION_DECISIONS_2026_05_11.md`, line 29) while its judge check replayed a single row (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`, line 284). The note contradicts itself on the count: line 25 says all 24 were service errors, while line 27 says 2 of the 24 were genuine failures; the result note agrees with 22 and 2 (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_v20a_lr1e4_result.md`, line 41). A missing file does not make a claim false: a later review found the cited collapse real on other grounds (`icloud-work/aptraining/handover/2026-05-01_session_end/SHADOW_HANDOVER.md`). The project's validation note argued that passes served from cached content were acceptable, since that content had once passed the live judge (`icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/validated/2026-05-22T2116Z_den_solver_v8_FIRST_VALIDATED/VALIDATION_REASON.md`). A response in the wrong shape is a failure of the delivered item, not missing evidence (`icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/full-copy/parallel-ideas-lab/reports/WEEKLY_APUSH_PIL_REPORT_20260520.md`). A skip because data is unavailable keeps the score and adds a caveat (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/tests/test_factual_audit_skipped_scoring.py`, line 75); the fact audit fails open, scoring 1.0, when no reference passages come back (commit 8aedb57); other errors are still tolerated as transient (commit 101e555); and the AP context path still returns an empty context with only a log line on an unknown curriculum, missing skills, no match, a course mismatch or any error (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/evaluators/base.py`, lines 759-821). Those tests use synthetic observations: the gate checks case ids, status and nonblank evidence text, not whether the evidence is a genuine measurement (`grade3-reading/artifacts/codex-qa/tool-reuse-assessment-2026-09-14.md`). Timeouts cluster on long outputs: the other item types timed out on 1-6% of calls (`feedback_ib_grader_v266_dbq_mcqset_timeout_99pct_at_concurrency_default_2026_06_02.md`, line 7). Unreadable output is the item's own failure when the format is part of the task, as when training on 262 answer-format rows left 0 of 150 outputs parseable (`project_eval_is_question_generation.md`, line 56), so such outcomes are counted apart, not dropped. A missing file can be a sync delay rather than a false claim (`feedback_eval_runs_sync_to_icloud.md`, line 31). For missing curriculum context the same evaluator keeps going instead: on a transient error it fails open and degrades to an empty context. Scores that do not apply are now stored as 1.0, with a separate flag as the authoritative signal, so an average that includes them reads them as passes. The lab sometimes counted the other way, treating score errors as failures, and leaving failures out is safe only with the completion rate reported beside the pass rate, as the same contract's four separate metrics do. The promoting note argued that the predictor was grader-backed: "the cached archetype is itself derived from live-IB-validated v80bchain content, so it's not "deterministic-from-bank" in the prior sense." (icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/validated/2026-05-22T2116Z_den_solver_v8_FIRST_VALIDATED/VALIDATION_REASON.md, line 62). Only the question-set runs slipped through: the short-answer and document-based runs held to the same bar carried returned ratings. Practice drifted from this: "6 fails (5 INFERIOR + 1 None) are real IB rejections." (aptraining-local/den-of-ideation/reports/validation_triage/20260524T071351Z_2026-05-24T0713Z_UNIT1_DBQ_SOLVER_VALIDATED.md.md, line 113) counted a row with no rating as a grader rejection. All 101 errors in the 480-item run came from a difficulty level the test plan requested but the generator never supported (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/benchmark_runs/PARTIAL_RESULTS_SUMMARY.md`, line 26), so they are a fault in the request more than in the generator, and the project left infrastructure errors out on purpose (`icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/CHANGELOG.md`, line 171: "- 503 errors from Gemini excluded from pass rate (infrastructure issue, not quality)"). Reporting both rates covers both cases. A deployed question generator does the opposite to stay available: it retries until success and falls back to extracting JSON by hand (`icloud-work/incept/question-generator-api/docs/GOALS.md`, `icloud-work/incept/question-generator-api/docs/ISSUES.md`). That serves a live service, not an evaluation.

### Planning maps are for adults

Treat a curriculum planning map as a guide for adults: never copy its rows into student material without separate review, or take a row as proof of learning. All 189 review-comment cells in one draft ledger are blank, which records no comments, not approval.

The routing packet for review feedback on the reading course says to treat the draft science workbook's rows as a candidate adult-facing coherence map, not approved student wording or proof that a student has already learned a concept (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/README.md`). Draft ledgers for several grades carry the same boundary: one is not evidence that younger students learned its concepts, another warns never to assume its concepts were taught, mastered, reviewed or approved, and a third forbids turning its statements into student prose without a separate authoring and review process (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0152-science-g8-atom-composite-ledger.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0149-draft-grade-5-science-ledger.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0150-science-g6-atom-composite-ledger.qmd`). The passage-integrity checks forbid copying a draft workbook sentence into child-facing prose without separate review, and the cross-subject guidance notes that the draft science standards are written for adults and do not reflect the language students will be given (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/science-passage-agent.md`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0137-science-social-studies-reencounter-guidance.qmd`). Rows copied into student material need separate authoring as well as review, and a row is no proof that a student was even taught it.

### Point every check at its own unit

Before checking a unit, confirm the grade, subject and reference files the check uses are that unit's own, since a check pointed at another unit's says nothing about this one. Checked against a replaced unit's files, every passage would have shown a 100% mismatch.

A Grade 5 adversarial review found that its brief cited the canonical files of the unit's superseded subject; comparing the rebuilt literary unit against them would have produced a 100% spurious mismatch on every passage and claim, so the run used the unit's current design source instead. A convergence review of a Grade 3 reading grader found its grade hardcoded to 11, carried over from AP US History.

That is not a useful canon-fidelity check.”

### Proofread every line students meet

Proofread every line a student reads or hears, model answers first, since validators miss grammar slips and the repeated stock openers of machine writing. One course repeated two stock openers across 11 think-alouds, and no validator caught it.

Two proofreading sweeps on 2026-08-31 read only the surface prose of every string a child sees or hears, leaving out whatever a validator already owns (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0233-aug31-sweeps-prose-and-slotmap.qmd`). In one course the worst finding was in a spoken model answer, the kind a child imitates: a subject-verb error repeated at 5 paths; in the other, every think-aloud in one unit opened with the same clause and every one in a second unit with another, 11 verbatim repetitions in all, and none of the findings is caught by any current validator (the same file). A slip that recurred at one slot was recommended as one fix to its template, not four patches (the same file). An earlier course review found word-bank prompts that misuse vocabulary and read as unedited AI output (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0086-round2-feedback-brainlifts-2026-07-09.qmd`).

### Prove a delay before claiming it

Call a check delayed only when the time that passed is recorded and proves the delay, because success on the same day shows short-term memory, not learning. A unit planned a 24-hour delay before its checkpoint, but the platform did not enforce it and no elapsed time was captured.

A demo reading unit's 90% gate was verified, but the platform did not enforce the intended 24-hour delay and no elapsed-time evidence was captured, so it is not a verified delayed assessment (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/handoffs-2026-07-13/course-eval-layer/README.md`). The practice spec licenses "acquired at checkpoint" and adds "delayed" only when timestamp evidence proves the interval, and never counts release-day completion, since same-day testing measures working memory, not learning (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). It sharpens the rule that learning needs a later test on new items: the test has to be provably later.

Quoted:

### Prove coverage item by item

Prove coverage by counting how many lessons and items serve each required skill, reading each scored item against the standard's boundary, and treat a zero as a gap. All 82 sub-codes were covered at least once, but 61 of them were rated Low.

A reading course closed 15 zero-coverage sub-codes to 0 in three verification passes, checking every closure against the code's exact assessment boundary by reading the actual scored item, not relabelling a slot (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/CURRICULUM-REVIEW-STANDING-2026-08-17.md`). A gap analysis the next day found all 82 sub-codes covered at least once but 61 of 82 rated Low, most with one item each (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/GAP-ANALYSIS-2026-08-18.md`). Skills carried from an earlier grade were held out of placement, neither counted as coverage zeros nor fake-placed into slots they don't belong in (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/RULING-B-CARRIED-MASTERY.md`). Count from the current placements, and never put a skill in a slot it doesn't fit to close a gap.

### Provenance for every field

Record where each field came from, not only each record, marking model-inferred content as unsourced with its reasoning, because one record can mix official text with generated fields. In one course's 2,703 records, 43% had at least one generated field.

An audit of an AP curriculum store found records under one source tag whose statements were official but whose misconceptions and assessment boundaries had been filled in by a model, because the official framework doesn't publish them (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/feedback_field_level_provenance.md`, lines 12-21). Field-level tags were then added: in one course 43% of 2,703 records had a generated field, mostly dates and themes, with misconceptions, boundaries or objectives generated in 88 (3%) (line 29). It takes recording where every asset came from down to each field.

Quoted:

Different fields in the same record can have different provenance. A consumer that trains on the record as a unit will train on the LLM-generated fields as if they were authoritative.”

### Qualify judges blind

Qualify anyone whose judgments will set a standard on a fresh blind test, because familiarity is not qualification.

After two qualification rounds for people who would judge a reading gold set failed, the record says familiarity with the project is not automatic qualification: a new blind result must show competence. The role rule it recommends has two people review independently and blind, a third qualified person adjudicate and a fourth sign any release. An agent-routing plan for the same course adds that no lane can certify the whole course by itself. Keep reviewing, adjudicating and signing off in separate hands, so that no one, person or agent, certifies their own work.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0165-eppc-g3-reviewer-qualification-terminal-outcomes-human-next-gate.qmd` (113-114): “Familiarity with the project is not automatic qualification; the new blind result must demonstrate competence.”

### Qualify on boundary cases and twins

Qualify anyone whose labels will set a standard on boundary cases and their opposite-value twins, not only clear cases, since clear-case accuracy can hide shared boundary failures. Two candidates scored 9/10 on clear positives and nearest neighbours but 3/10 and 2/10 on boundary cases and 3/10 each on opposite-value cases.

A blind, synthetic 60-item qualification round tested whether two candidates could reproduce a frozen scheme for coding teaching principles into typed fields. Both scored 9/10 on positives and nearest neighbours and 10/10 on missingness and scope gaps, with structurally valid submissions, but 3/10 and 2/10 on boundary cases and 3/10 each on reciprocal cases, the same effect with the opposite value. Fifteen of their sixteen shared failures had identical failed field signatures, which the round read as a gap in protocol and competence rather than random noise.

### Rank findings by their effect on learners

Rank findings by effect on learners: anything that can mislead, falsely reject, block or wrongly advance a learner holds the work, polish comes last, and preferences aren't defects.

The Grade 5 instruction-review profile ranks findings by what they do to learners (`grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/courses/g5-reading/review/generated/instruction-review-profile.json`, lines 129-133). Its top priority blocks bounded review because a learner can be misled, falsely rejected, unable to complete the intended work or given invalid progression; the next must be corrected before external submission because instruction, feedback or transfer is materially weaker than the intended design; presentation polish comes last and cannot override either.

### Read a worked example without its text

Test a worked example by reading it with the source sentences hidden: if what remains reads as a list of correct answers, it models answers, not thinking, and fails.

An authoring contract for a Grade 3 reading course bans the question, quote, answer pattern in its worked example, because that labels answers and does not model thinking, and asks each step to show what the reader asks, where they look, a candidate checked or a wrong turn caught, and why the answer matters. Its self-check before a lesson is done reads the worked example with the passage sentences hidden: if it still reads as a list of correct answers, it fails, and is rewritten until the reasoning is the content.

### Read the failures, not the average

After every change, read the failing items and compare them with the baseline's item by item, because an unchanged average or pass rate can hide new failures. A new version fixed all 9 of the old one's failures and failed 11 new items, with no item failing in both.

When one AP model was retrained, its pass rate fell from 85.0% to 81.7%, two items on its set, yet no item failed in both versions: the new one fixed all 9 of the old one's failures and introduced 11 new ones (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/BEADS.md`). On another day, reading the failures showed all 26 were content failures with no parse failure among them, so the plan recorded that three fixes aimed at output format and examples had all addressed the wrong failure mode (`icloud-work/aptraining/.agent/memory/FINAL_PLAN_2026_05_11_v3.md`). Read the checks each failing item failed, and compare before naming a cause: an unchanged total can hide a new kind of failure or an item type that broke.

### Readability by sentence, not by formula

When long words, such as a taught word, lift a readability score, judge whether an item reads too hard by its sentence length and clause depth instead. Options of single-clause sentences of 9–15 words were flagged because their long words lifted the formula score.

A content audit for Grade 3 reading lessons flags a question that reads materially harder than its passage by a readability formula, but on vocabulary items the taught word is long on purpose and lifts the score without making the sentence hard, so its instructions say to judge sentence length and clause depth there instead (`shadow/content-eval/SKILL.md`). Three lesson reviews set formula flags aside on that ground: single-clause options of 9–15 words, sentences of 12–18 words at most one clause deep, and options of about 15–18 words with one clause each (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L12-review.md`, `shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L13-review.md`, `shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L14-review.md`).

Quoted:

- `shadow-content-eval/SKILL.md` (112-115): “On those items judge **sentence length and clause depth**, not the score — a 24-word option with an embedded `because` clause against a grade-4 passage is a real problem; four short sentences carrying one long target word is not.”
- `shadow-content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L12-review.md` (132): “- **READABILITY on p2c, p3c and p4c:** the options are single-clause sentences of 9–15 words. The inflated FK score comes from polysyllabic words, not clause depth.”

### Rebuild when the premise is rejected

When review rejects a draft's premise, rebuild on the corrected premise instead of polishing the same design, and never revive a rejected concept because its code exists.

Early drafts of a Grade 9 unit opening were rejected as too childish, too like a guide-led dashboard, or too like an app showing images rather than a storytelling experience; the 6 October handover records that criticism as a design correction, not a request for more decorative polish on the same premise, and says not to resurrect those concepts simply because code exists (line 62). It names another visually polished deliverable that solves the wrong problem as the largest creative risk (line 483).

Quoted:

- `g9-archive/handover-2026-10-06/Othello-handover-docs-and-transcript-2026-10-06.zip` (Othello-handover/Othello-project-handover.txt inside it) (62): “Do not resurrect those concepts simply because code exists.”

- `g9-archive/handover-2026-10-06/Othello-handover-docs-and-transcript-2026-10-06.zip` (Othello-handover/Othello-project-handover.txt inside it) (483): “The largest creative risk is another visually polished deliverable that solves the wrong problem.”

Against: The same handover sets a limit: open choices are to be decided with real evidence when they matter, and they are not a reason to discard existing work or reopen settled creative decisions (line 489). ### Recalibrate bars before reusing them

Don't carry pass bars, yields or thresholds measured on one course or grade over to another; recalibrate them on a control set there first.

The bars and yields at hand for a grade 3 reading course had been derived from a grade 5 one, and the practice spec makes a grade 3 recalibration control set a blocking precondition before any grade 3 gate or generation budget goes live, since historical grade 5 volume does not validate a grade 3 estimate (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`). The grade 3 practice criteria repeat it for every threshold and yield (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/g3-reading-red-team/references/dimensions/D6-practice-durable-mastery.md`).

### Recompute what arrives with content

Never trust a pass label or measured value that arrives with content, such as a certification, a length, a reading level or a verbatim flag; recompute it on arrival. A 12-row pilot certified as passing on every row came out 6 pass and 6 fail on local structural checks.

A review of another reading project's proxy test found it trusted the generator's own word counts and reading levels and a 30-character substring check for verbatim spans, which paraphrase defeats; the action adopted was to recompute them at intake and treat any self-reported field used as a gate as unverified (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0072-learnings-from-incept-map-proxy-2026-06-25.qmd`). A received Grade 5 pilot of 12 rows carried embedded certification of pass for anti-leak and MAP-likeness on every row, yet local structural checks passed 6 and failed 6, and an independent passage-blind check was still required (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0067-g5-generator-pilot-intake-and-team-async-2026-06-23.qmd`).

### Record where every asset came from

Record where every asset came from and its hash, check the hash before using it, and treat a source note as a record of origin, not a licence to reuse.

Each video frame takes its pictures by id and SHA-256, verified before use, and an asset's source note records its
origin, not a right to reuse it (`unit-video-modules/INTEGRATION.md`); the lesson engine checks each painting's bytes
against its manifest before drawing it (`g9/transformer/src/video/art.js`), and every film it makes carries a manifest
of module digests, narrator, renderer versions and file hashes (`g9/transformer/src/video/produce.js`). The kit's
narration rule keeps one folder per model, voice and direction, because a new voice in an old folder leaves old takes
under a new label (`othello-unit-video/.claude/skills/uvk-narration-make/SKILL.md`).

### Record why the checks missed it

With every confirmed defect, record why the existing checks missed it, so the gap in the checks is fixed along with the item.

A lesson audit's workflow requires every issue to record, besides its symptom, reproduction, expected behaviour, cause and cause confidence, why earlier checks missed it, and each finding record carries a priorTestGap field for it. Two of its findings show what the field catches: a test suite that tested one grade's isolated branch but expressly allowed the unisolated branch and never exercised the other grade's caller, and a question whose tests checked only the key's index and so never tested a competing interpretation. Naming the gap points the repair at the checks as well as at the item.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md` (46): “Every issue records its visible symptom, minimal reproduction, expected behavior and source, affected pages, code mechanism, cause confidence, and why earlier checks missed it.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md` (73): “`affectedScope`, `priorTestGap`, `proposedFix`”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (663): “The earlier suite tested the isolated branch but expressly allowed the unisolated branch; it never exercised the Grade 3 caller.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/BEAD-REGISTER.json` (3052): “Cause: the question omitted the comparison group; answer-index testing alone never tests competing interpretations.”

### Refuse to check a half-written file

Before checking a file, confirm it is whole, such as ending where it must and holding its anchors, and refuse otherwise, because a truncated copy can pass every assertion. Cut to 98% of its length, a file passed all 78 of an audit's assertions; cut to 70%, it failed 29.

A Grade 3 reading build's patch scripts truncate a file and then write it, so a check that reads during a write gets a prefix, and its rulebook notes that a prefix scans cleanly. Measured on one audit by cutting the file: at 70% it failed 29 assertions, at 98% it reported all 78 passing with no sign anything was wrong, and at 95% it lost five call sites and still passed its census. That audit and a copy-editing check now refuse to run unless the file ends in its closing html tag and carries its anchor functions, deliberately not a size band, which would need editing at every change, and the rule is to believe a refusal over a green run.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (552): “ALL 78 PASS with no sign anything was wrong”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (549-550): “so an overlapping read returns a *prefix* — and a prefix scans cleanly”
- `grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md` (553-554): “now refuse (exit 2) unless the file ends in `</html>` and carries its anchor functions”

Against: The incident that first prompted the rule was traced to a load-order race in the player rather than a partial read, and "a mid-write read and a load-order race present identically" while needing opposite fixes (grade3-reading/edullm-review-hub/course-packages/archive/g3-reading-v4/content-for-analysis/BUILD-RULES.md, line 545); the truncation hazard itself rests on the deliberate cutting test.

### Remake under new rules

When a rule changes, remake what was made under the old rule instead of serving it.

Each block's key includes the maker's version and its kind's version, so a changed prompt or check makes the block
again instead of serving the old one (`g9/transformer/src/blocks.js`); the render and playtest routes take a block only
under the key today's rules make (`g9/transformer/src/server.js`, `g9/transformer/test/server.test.mjs`).

### Render the extremes at every width

Render a course's extremes, its longest word, option and sentence and its largest set of options, at phone, tablet and desktop widths, and again whenever new content extends one. A desktop-only check battery missed all three classes of layout fault one visual audit found.

The reading project's QC checklist asks that the longest word, longest option, longest sentence and largest option count render clean at 1280 and 390 pixels, again whenever new content extends an extreme, and at a third width in the 720 to 820 pixel band, which its walker never opened (`grade3-reading/artifacts/AlphaRead-QC-Checklist-v2-2026-09-04.md`). A visual audit found three faults, among them long button labels that overflowed the 390 pixel viewport and forced sideways scrolling, and the register's class rule was that the check battery was desktop-only, so all three were invisible to it (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-codex-visual-2026-09-07/REGISTER.md`).

### Repeated generic comments mean unobserved pages

Treat identical generic comments across reviewed pages as false coverage: mark those pages unobserved and review each again, asking what the learner has read or heard and must do.

A lesson audit's workflow names false coverage as its first failure mode and lists its signs: missing page or state evidence, identical generic comments, a screenshot never reviewed, and a source or HTTP check described as a student attempt. Its recovery is to mark the page unobserved, perform the browser action and replace the claim with a precise coverage limit. Each page review reads the visible text, inspects the screenshot and asks what the learner has actually read or heard, what they should do and why the offered control is valid there. The workflow cites the project's pattern that evidence defeats rubber-stamp review.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md` (93): “Detect: missing page/state evidence, identical generic comments, screenshot never reviewed, HTTP/source assertion described as a student attempt.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md` (93): “Recovery: 1. mark unobserved; 2. perform browser action; 3. replace claim with precise coverage limit.”
- `grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md` (44): “Read the actual visible text, inspect the screenshot, and ask: what has the learner actually read/heard, what should they do, and why is the offered control valid here?”

### Replace failed items, then recheck coverage

Take every item a check or filter fails out of what learners see and replace it, not just exclude it from scoring, then recheck skill and format coverage. One course went out with 231 of 772 items it had classed as answerable without the text still live.

An adversarial review of the Grade 5 submission found 231/772 items (29.9%) classified as known-leaky, excluded from the gate instruments but not removed from the live course (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/redteam-sources/g5-reading-redteam-round1-2026-07-06.md`, line 17), and the course formula drew the lesson that a leaky item awards progress for not reading (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`, line 233). The same review found all 20 two-part evidence items in the excluded bucket, so six-format coverage quietly became five-format on the certified core (the review, line 27). An excluded item still rewards skipping the work, and a filter that is right item by item can drop a whole skill or format.

### Replaced content gets a new identity

When an item, its rubric or a lesson is changed or replaced, give it a new identity, so old answers, verdicts, progress and art don't attach to it.

Rebuilt Grade 5 lessons that reused the old lesson IDs inherited unrelated completion and artwork from the lessons they replaced. The integration rule that followed requires identity changes across progress, session state, unit introduction and asset fallback, keeping the old records without applying them to the new content, and the release checklist bars legacy IDs from preserving mastery for replacement content. The restoration plan had named the danger beforehand: with identical IDs both the unit and lesson lookups would prefer the old content, and art keyed by lesson ID could survive new text.

### Report each readiness gate on its own

Report each readiness gate on its own, with how it was verified and what is still open, never averaging gates or letting one stand in for another. One course was 100% authored while its other readiness gates stood at 0%.

A locally authored AP course was reported as 100% authored, with human content review, source and rights review, accessibility review, independent item certification and runtime verification each at 0%, and its ledger says not to average those gates into a single quality score; the zero rows are later acceptance gates, not missing lessons. A plan to centralise the reading standards makes missing required data produce a not-evaluable verdict that names the missing inputs and blocks any completion claim. A reading release's deployment proof states that it proves only one part's vertical slice. The gates run from file checks and the live player to rights, accessibility, certification and human review, and missing evidence counts as not evaluable.

### Report every defect in one pass

Record every defect a check finds, even when the item has already failed for another reason, and keep evaluating, so everything can be fixed in one round. A section yielding only one word is reported, because a list that short is more likely to be a bad read than a real lesson.

A code check for references to a neighbouring lesson was at first not recorded when the judge had already failed the same score for another reason, so its defect would surface only after the first issue was fixed; it is now recorded whenever found, with the judge's reasoning kept. The project's research summary reports a lesson with no vocabulary section as content to add, and a section yielding only one word the same way, in the final report beside what is good, bad and missing, and neither stops the rest of the evaluation. It rejects halting a run on a missing section, which would trade one finding for all the others. Every missing or suspiciously thin part is recorded the same way.

Quoted:

- `shadow-bench/` (commit a8818e0) (27-30): “- Record the relational-reference defect whenever refs are found, even when the LLM had already failed structure_compliance for another reason (preserve its reasoning) so the N2 defect is discoverable in the same pass instead of only after the first issue is fixed.”
- `shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md` (36): “**Report what is missing or suspiciously thin, and carry on.**”
- `shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md` (36): “A lesson with no vocabulary section is a finding sent back to the generator team as content to add.”
- `shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md` (36): “A section yielding only one word is reported the same way, because a list that short is more likely to be a bad read than a real lesson.”
- `shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md` (36): “Neither stops the rest of the evaluation (DOK1-15).”
- `shadow-bench/docs/brainlift.md` (84): “Halting the run would trade one finding for all the others.”

### Report pass rate and mean

Report the mean score beside the pass rate, fixing in advance which decides, because a pass cut turns small shifts near the bar into noise or false gains. On one item type the pass rate rose from 20.0% to 43.3% while the mean score fell from 0.779 to 0.732.

After one change to an AP model, the clean per-type table showed the mean score falling on 3 of 10 item types, and on 2 of them the pass rate rose at the same time, one by a single item (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_v20a_lr1e4_result.md`, lines 21-32). The grader's overall scores fall in a few clusters, 0.75-0.84 just below the fixed 0.85 threshold and 0.85-0.99 just above, so more items can clear it while the near-misses score lower (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/reference_inceptbench.md`, line 82). An earlier note in the same result file put the fall at 7 of 10 types, from scoring that counted lost items as zeros (line 42). Fix in advance which of the two decides.

### Report the number that was measured

Report every result as measured on real output, misses included and never rounded across its bar, recomputed from primary records; a projected, templated or summary-copied figure is no result. A calibration set cited as having about 150 responses had 48.

Audits of an assessment's approval case found summary tables showing reliability as "0.930 ✅" against a ≥0.93 benchmark where the reports beneath them said 0.928, and the one failing metric (RMSE 4.12 vs <4.0 target) left out of every summary table (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/00_AUDITS_AND_FIXES.md`). A red-team pass on a writing course's package found a reused calibration set cited as "48 items, ~150 banded kid responses" that was 12 items and 48 responses, a number inherited from a research agent's summary and not recomputed before it was written down (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g4g5-writing/approval-package/RED_TEAM_R1.md`), and one grade's certified count drifted 541 vs 549 vs 559 across documents. The course plans' rules since: every number carries a source and comes off one dated pull, no magnitude is carried from another grade or cohort, one grade's bars and yields need a recalibration set before they gate another, and an unknown cell is marked [TO SOURCE], never invented (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/course-formula-agents.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`, `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/grade-band-profiles.md`). Never round a near miss across its bar, leave out a failing metric or copy a number from a summary, and mark a number not yet measured as unsourced.

### Report the ready and the whole cohort

When learners arrive with gaps a course doesn't own, report outcomes both for the cohort without those gaps and for the whole cohort, never only one.

A grade 7 and 8 prealgebra design, facing learners' debt in earlier-grade prerequisites and fluency, leads with a diagnostic map of that debt and always reports two numbers: outcomes for the native cohort and for the full cohort (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7g8-prealgebra/brainlifts/v0.1.md`, line 26). Quoting only the native cohort is cherry-picking, and quoting only the full cohort punishes the course for earlier-grade debt it doesn't own.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7g8-prealgebra/brainlifts/v0.1.md` (26): “reports two numbers always: native-cohort outcomes and full-cohort outcomes. A course that only quotes the native cohort is cherry-picking; one that only quotes the full cohort punishes itself for K–6 debt it doesn't own.”
- `grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g7g8-prealgebra/brainlifts/v0.1.md` (26): “The course leads with the diagnostic/debt map”

Against: none found

<sub>method · stage: measure · measurement, evidence-of-learning · universal · from g3 · adopted-rule · held · found in [2026-10-12-5-full-crawl](../research/2026-10-12-5-full-crawl/)</sub>

### Rerun every check after any fix

After any change or fix, re-run every check and quality measure on the whole set, passed items included, because a fix for one can break another. A speaker-label fix passed a 1466/1466 live battery and still turned the full suite red.

In the reading project, a speaker-label fix passed every targeted check, including a machine re-listen, walkers and a 1466/1466 live battery, and still turned the full check suite red, because a validator comparing the exact field it touched ran nowhere in the listening pipeline. Each targeted verifier reads one slice of the contract, so any edit to the course file now runs the full suite on the final tree before commit. Re-run after any change, not only a fix, with no check switched off, add a fresh balanced set, and look for new kinds of failure.

The reports do not say what each update changed, so which change caused which effect is not known. The judge flips verdicts on identical generations ("The InceptBench evaluator has a **20% rating-flip rate** on identical generations across 4 repeated trials.", `icloud-work/ap-social-studies-generator/python/CLAUDE.md`, line 101), so control regressions of 5.1% to 9.0% against a 3% limit may be judge noise rather than real regressions, and a limit set below the judge's noise reverts every change. The control samples were small (`--control-pct 15`, the same file, line 192). The source is a proposal and reports no result of this test (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0128-externalized-pedagogy-policy-compiler-decision.qmd`). The same change was a real gain on multiple choice (`project_richer_rag_per_cell_tradeoff.md`, line 19). The full-set run compared fresh outputs with a stored baseline, which by itself moved short answers by 3.60 points (`feedback_baseline_must_be_fresh_gen.md`, line 24), so part of the drop may be that artifact. the faults it names are in a course package's documents and counts, not in its items. The report doesn't say how many changes the run made, so it shows that a fix for one dimension can break others, not that making one change at a time avoids it. A later run found: a planned editor stage would re-check only a step a person edits by hand, not every check on the whole set (`g9/transformer/v03/README.md`). A later run found counter-evidence (`grade3-reading/ui-audit-2026-09-08/WORKFLOW.md`).

### Resolve every cited page to its id

Before acting on feedback, resolve each page it cites to the page's stable id, from its link or by matching its on-screen text, since delivery surfaces number pages differently. An old link to page 5 opens the page whose id is p4, because the count includes an opening video.

A reading course delivers each lesson on two surfaces that name the same page differently. On one, a page's address is its authored id, but old links that give a page number still resolve by position, so `?page=5` lands on `/p4`, the fifth page counting the opening video (`grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md`, lines 25-29); the other prepends a welcome page and one page per unit film on a unit's first lesson, so its 'page 3' is often the lesson's first page (lines 30-36). The course's procedure for taking in feedback therefore resolves every cited link or screenshot to the lesson and page id before registering it, matches a screenshot's on-screen text into the lesson's data when there is no link, and records both forms and which surface the feedback came from (lines 19-23 and 35-44).

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md` (35-37): “the book's "page 3" is often the lesson's p0 — NEVER count dots or "page N" words from a reviewer; resolve to the id in the URL bar or, for a screenshot with no URL, match the on-screen text into the lesson JSON”
- `grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md` (26-29): “Legacy ?page=<n> still resolves, by POSITION, into the path form (verified live: ?page=5 lands on /p4, the 5th page counting the video opener p0) — so a ?page=N link in old feedback is a position, not an id.”
- `grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md` (39-40): “A reviewer phrase like "the vocab page" or "page 5 of 13" is AMBIGUOUS across surfaces”
- `grade3-reading/.claude/skills/reviewer-round/SKILL.md` (22-23): “Resolve each cited link/screenshot to `lessonId + page id` before registering, and record BOTH forms in the register row”

Against: none found

### Retire items, don't delete them

Retire an item instead of deleting it, and record what it was merged into or is now covered by, so every change can be traced. One standards workbook keeps its retired standards on a tab of their own, each marked with what it was merged into, covered by or rewritten as.

A standards workbook's version summary lists its retired standards as preserved for traceability, and its retired tab marks each with what it was merged into, covered by or rewritten as (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx`). A count made in this run found the summary's 11 retired standards against 9 rows on that tab, so the trace itself has to be checked against its data.

- `downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx` (sheet 'V7.0 Executive Summary', cell A65): “- RETIRED standards: 11 (preserved for traceability)”

### Review as a student

Review a lesson in the mode students get: one player's reviewer mode let a seek skip its checks, and the students' mode never did.

Notes on another build's film player said a seek skipped its checks; in its live code that was true only in reviewer
mode, and learners had no forward seek, so both notes were corrected (`g9/review/three-film-comparison/COMPARISON.md`,
"Corrections made in this pass").

### Review each item after real use

Once items are in use, review each one's statistics as a standing duty, and revise, quarantine or retire those that fail.

The assessment packet requires a live-analysis plan covering a minimum number of students, item and option functioning, subgroup and differential item functioning review, uncertainty, drift, quarantine and retirement (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/assessment-item-agent.md`). The project's digest of a national reading study sets the bar: if performance differences reflect individual, social, linguistic or cultural variation rather than comprehension, the test is inadequate (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`; RAND Reading Study Group 2002, https://www.rand.org/pubs/monograph_reports/MR1465.html). Revise options almost nobody picks, investigate items where weaker students beat stronger ones or stronger ones favour a distractor, and check subgroup fairness and drift.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/assessment-item-agent.md` (55-56): “Live-analysis plan covering minimum N, item and option functioning, subgroup/DIF review, uncertainty, drift, quarantine, and retirement.”
- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd` (753): “Good comprehension assessments must be adaptable to individual, social, linguistic, and cultural variation; if performance differences reflect such variation rather than comprehension itself, the test is inadequate for the research/instructional agenda.”

<sub>method · stage: measure · measurement, accessibility · universal · from g3, research · adopted-rule · held · found in [2026-10-12-4-deep-sweep](../research/2026-10-12-4-deep-sweep/), [2026-10-12-5-full-crawl](../research/2026-10-12-5-full-crawl/)</sub>

### Review in rounds, each with a new lens

Review in rounds, each through a new lens and again after every change, fixes and display code included, and stop only after two rounds in a row find nothing new. On one set of nine lessons, successive rounds found 5, 5, 5, 1 and 1 critical faults before a round found none.

One course's review loop changed its lens each round; its lenses included a walk as a student who gets everything right and one who gets every gated item wrong twice, a line-by-line check against the source lessons, a simulated first read by someone outside the project, and a comparison with a course already shipped. On the same nine lessons the first five rounds found 5, 5, 5, 1 and 1 critical faults, and the sixth, run on what had changed, found none (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R2.md` and the later rounds beside it). After the content had converged, 8 new engine commits brought a round that found two critical faults, and the loop's rule then sent the fix commit itself to fresh eyes; an earlier round had found a fix that solved its target while breaking a field it didn't need to touch.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R2.md` (4): “(a) gets everything right, (b) gets every gated item wrong twice before recovering.”

- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R2.md` (276): “| CRITICAL | 5 (doubled phrase in U1-L4 wedo;”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-19-R3.md` (19): “Totals: **5 CRITICAL / 2 WORTH-FIXING / 1 POLISH.**”

- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R6.md` (12): “**Result: ZERO CRITICALs.** No CRITICAL findings on the changed surface.”
- `grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-21-R8.md` (10): “*content* surface; this round exists because 8 new engine commits landed after R7's base.”

Against: Re-review is scoped to what changed: by the loop's rule, "a lens never runs twice on unchanged content" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW-2026-08-20-R6.md`, lines 9-10).

### Rewrite whatever is reused

Anything reused from another lesson or item, such as a check, step names, narration or a feedback line, must be rewritten for its new place. One narration line that made no sense was the same string in three lessons.

Hand reviews traced defects to pieces carried over from elsewhere: a quick check from a lesson on another skill, which taught the wrong skill; guided practice under another lesson's step names; a narration line that made no sense and was the same string in three lessons; and a feedback line that invented a story detail by copying a sentence from an earlier item.

<sub>method · stage: write · alignment, integrity · universal · from g3 · measured · held · found in [2026-10-12-4-deep-sweep](../research/2026-10-12-4-deep-sweep/), [2026-10-12-5-full-crawl](../research/2026-10-12-5-full-crawl/)</sub>

### Run a fixed smoke set first

Before any full run and after every change, run a small fixed smoke set end to end, and use it to find bugs, not to estimate rates. A five-item probe surfaces format collapse and breakage for about 3% of a full run's cost.

Two builds burned full 150-row grading runs before their collapse showed, one with 0 of 150 parsing and one 16.2 points down, so the project required a five-item smoke first: one item per type, drawn from the held-out pool and fixed across runs so results compare. A later backlog turns each recurring failure family into 3 to 5 fixed regression prompts run locally and live after every deploy, after five deploys had each carried an unverified gain claim. The set holds one item of each type plus a few per known failure family and runs through the whole make-and-check path.

Quoted:

- `icloud-work/aptraining/coordination/scripts/SHIP_PRECONDITIONS.md` (76-78): “v38 (262 rows, eval=0/150 parse_ok) and v39 (1036 rows, −16.2pp binary) both burned the full 150-row IB-grader run before their collapse was visible.”
- `icloud-work/aptraining/coordination/scripts/SHIP_PRECONDITIONS.md` (79-80): “A 5-item probe surfaces format collapse, deployment-side breakage, and obvious regressions for ~3% of the cost.”
- `icloud-work/aptraining/coordination/scripts/SHIP_PRECONDITIONS.md` (82-85): “**Smoke composition.** 5 APUSH items, one per cell type (`MCQ`, `MCQ_SET`, `SAQ`, `DBQ`, `LEQ`), drawn from the held-out eval pool (NOT the training set). Items are fixed across runs so smoke results are comparable;”
- `icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/evidence/FUTURE_RUN_IMPROVEMENT_BACKLOG_20260521.md` (209): “- Convert each family into 3-5 fixed regression prompts.”
- `icloud-work/aptraining-crystal-copy-20260521/evidence/FUTURE_RUN_IMPROVEMENT_BACKLOG_20260521.md` (210): “- Run them locally and live after every deploy.”

### Run a proven check on every real item

Run every check on every real item before a generated set feeds anything that matters, not on a sample or only on the fixtures it was proven on. A readiness audit verified code, hashes and structure without applying the screen to the 120 real spans.

In a qualification round for a reading gold set, public tests proved that a privacy screen rejected adversarial fixtures and accepted synthetic safe rows, and the final readiness audit verified code, hashes and structure, but nothing applied the screen itself to all 120 real spans; the record calls these different claims. When the screen was finally run on the would-be public rows, at least one span matched and the round failed closed. Record what each check found.

Quoted:

- `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0165-eppc-g3-reviewer-qualification-terminal-outcomes-human-next-gate.qmd` (81): “predicate to all 120 final private spans. Those are different claims.”
